definition_zh: 公开地；不隐瞒地；当众；坦率地
definition_en: in a way that does not hide facts, feelings or intentions and can be seen or heard by other people
core_image: 一扇原本关着的窗被推开，屋里的东西全暴露在日光下
scene: 会议进行到一半，一位年轻工程师站起来，把项目失败的原因一条条讲出来，没有替任何人遮掩。 He spoke openly about the delays that had ruined the schedule.
sceneCN: 这里是「公开地、不隐瞒地」（第 1 个义项：不掩饰事实或态度）；句意为他把拖垮进度的延误坦然讲了出来。图中可辨识物件：推开的窗、照进屋内的日光、摊开的文件。

pos.zh: 公开地；不隐瞒地；当众；坦率地

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 open 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「公开；坦率；开阔」
由动词 open 加 -ing 构成，义为「开口；开幕；空缺职位」
由 open 加表示「做某事的人或物」的 -er 构成，义为「开启者；开瓶器」

senses.title: Without hiding the facts
senses.definition: in a way that lets other people see or know the facts instead of keeping them secret
senses.definitionCN: 让他人看到或知道事实，而不是把事实藏起来
senses.example: She openly admitted that the first draft had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她公开承认初稿失败了。
senses.why: Open describes something not shut and not covered, so acting openly means leaving the facts uncovered for anyone to look at.
senses.whyCN: open 形容没有关闭、没有遮盖的东西，所以 openly 做事就是把事实摊开任人查看，而不是盖上一块布。

senses.title: In front of other people
senses.definition: in public, where other people can see or hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合，别人能够看见或听见所发生的事
senses.example: The two ministers openly disagreed in front of the press.
senses.exampleCN: 两位部长在记者面前公开表示意见不合。
senses.why: If nothing is covered, the act cannot stay private, so the same picture of an open space turns into doing something in public.
senses.whyCN: 既然没有遮盖，这个动作就留不住私密性；同一种「空间敞开」的画面，自然转到「当众做事」的含义上。

senses.title: Frankly, with feelings shown
senses.definition: in a direct way that shows real feelings or intentions without disguise
senses.definitionCN: 直接表达真实情感或意图，不加伪装
senses.example: They openly wept when the old theatre was pulled down.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老剧院被拆时，他们毫不掩饰地哭了。
senses.why: The image stretches from objects to feelings: a face that hides nothing is as open as a door that has never been locked.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象从物体延伸到情感：一张不藏东西的脸，就像一扇从没上过锁的门那样「敞开」。

intro.en: Openly is the adjective open plus the adverb suffix -ly, so its history is the history of open, a native English and Germanic word rather than a Latin one.
intro.cn: openly 就是形容词 open 加副词后缀 -ly，它的历史就是 open 的历史，而 open 是英语本土的日耳曼词，并非来自拉丁语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *upanaz is generally tied to the idea of being up or lifted, and it is the source of the English word for not shut.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *upanaz 与「向上、抬起」的意思相关，是英语中表示「未关闭」这个词的来源。

items.en: Old English already had open as an adjective for what is not closed, not covered or not blocked.
items.cn: 古英语里已有 open 这个形容词，表示未关闭、未遮盖或未被阻挡。

items.en: Middle English added -ly to adjectives to build adverbs, and openly appeared as the manner word for open action.
items.cn: 中古英语用 -ly 把形容词变成副词，openly 就这样出现，表示「以敞开的方式」。

items.en: The adverb moved from physical openings to speech, so saying something openly meant saying it with nothing concealed.
items.cn: 这个副词从物理上的敞开扩展到言语，说某事 openly 就是一点不隐瞒地说。

items.en: Modern English uses openly mainly for facts, feelings and public disagreement, and speak openly has become the usual pairing.
items.cn: 现代英语的 openly 主要用于事实、情感和公开的分歧，speak openly 已成为最常见的搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the open family and its spellings; the near-meaning group keeps adverbs that describe how plainly something is said or done.
note.cn: 形近组收 open 词族的同根词与不同拼写；近义组收同样描述「说得或做得有多直白」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind openly, meaning not closed and not hidden.
entries.definitionCN: openly 所由构成的形容词，义为未关闭、不隐瞒的。

entries.definition: A hole or gap, or the first performance of a show.
entries.definitionCN: 开口或缺口的；也指演出的首场。

entries.definition: The quality of being open, honest or free to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 公开、坦诚或可自由进入的性质。

entries.definition: Generous, with the hand open to give.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨大方的，手掌张开愿意给予。

entries.definition: In a direct and honest way, with no attempt to hide anything.
entries.definitionCN: 直接而诚实，不试图隐瞒任何东西。

entries.definition: In a place or manner that everyone can see or know.
entries.definitionCN: 在人人可见可知的场合或方式下。

entries.definition: Honestly, even when the truth makes people uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实地说，即使真相让人不舒服。

normalIntro.en: The word is open plus -ly, so every mnemonic hangs on the picture of something uncovered and on the small family built from the same adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 open 加 -ly，所以联想都围绕「没有遮盖」的画面，以及由同一形容词长出的那一小族词。

normal.en: Open means not shut, so openly means with nothing shut away.
normal.cn: open 是「没关上」，openly 就是「没把任何东西关起来藏住」。

normal.en: -ly turns the adjective into a manner, so an open act becomes an act done openly.
normal.cn: -ly 把形容词变成方式，于是 open 的动作就成了 openly 地做。

normal.en: Openness is the noun of the same family, naming the same quality as a thing.
normal.cn: openness 是同一词族的名词形式，把同一种性质当成一个东西来说。

normal.en: An opening is the place where something has been opened: a gap or a first night.
normal.cn: opening 是被打开的地方：一个缺口，或一场首演。

normal.en: Speak openly is the most common pairing, because speech is where hiding is easiest.
normal.cn: speak openly 是最常见的搭配，因为言语最容易把东西藏住。

abstract.en: A window pushed up in the morning: the room has nothing left to hide.
abstract.cn: 清晨把窗子推上去：屋子再没有可以藏的东西。

abstract.en: A closed hand keeps a secret, while an open hand must show what it holds.
abstract.cn: 握紧的手能藏住秘密，张开的手只能让人看见掌心里的东西。

abstract.en: Saying a hard truth openly costs more than saying an easy one quietly.
abstract.cn: 把难听的真相公开说出来，比轻声说一句好听话代价更大。

examples.en: She openly admitted that the first draft had failed.
examples.cn: 她公开承认初稿失败了。

examples.en: The committee openly rejected the proposal.
examples.cn: 委员会公开否决了这项提议。

examples.en: He prefers to speak openly rather than hint at problems.
examples.cn: 他宁愿把问题直说，也不愿只做暗示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧盆里」——盆盖一掀开，里面的东西全看得见；记住 openly 是公开地。

root: open 属英语本土的日耳曼词，一般认为来自重构词根 *upanaz（向上、抬起）；加 -ly 构成副词 openly，义为「以敞开、不遮掩的方式」。这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an uncovered surface, and the senses move from facts that are not hidden, to acts done in public, to feelings shown without disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有遮盖的表面」；义项从「不隐瞒的事实」移到「在人前做的事」，再到「不加伪装地流露情感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window pushed open so that everything inside stands in plain light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇被推开的窗，屋里的一切都摆在明处。

branches.en: a draft read aloud with the failed pages left in
branches.cn: 朗读稿子时把失败的页码照样留在里面

branches.en: a manager naming the delay instead of blaming the weather
branches.cn: 负责人直接点出延误，而不是怪天气

branches.en: two officials arguing in front of reporters
branches.cn: 两位官员在记者面前争论

branches.en: a face that will not look away while speaking
branches.cn: 说话时不肯把脸转开

branches.en: mourners weeping without turning aside
branches.cn: 送别的人不侧过脸就哭了出来

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective for not shut plus the English adverb suffix -ly, and the family around it adds nouns for the gap, the act and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「未关闭」的日耳曼语形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly 构成；它周围的一族词再用名词形式表示缺口、动作与性质。

latinIntro.en: Open is native English and Germanic, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: open 属英语本土的日耳曼词，这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: not closed, not covered, not hidden
items.meaningCN: 未关闭的；未遮盖的；不隐瞒的
items.example: The door was left open all night.

items.meaning: in a way that hides nothing
items.exampleCN: 他们公开讨论了这次损失。

items.example: Her openness made the meeting shorter.
items.exampleCN: 她的坦率让会议开得更短。

items.meaning: a gap or a first performance
items.example: The opening drew a full house.

items.meaning: a person or tool that opens
items.example: He borrowed an opener for the bottle.
items.exampleCN: 他借了个开瓶器开瓶子。

items.example: The envelope stayed unopened for a week.

items.meaning: someone or something with nothing to hide
items.example: His finances are an open book.
items.exampleCN: 他的财务状况一目了然。

definition_zh: 意外的；出乎意料的；没有料想到的；突兀的
definition_en: not anticipated or planned, so that it surprises people
core_image: 推开门发现屋里站着一位本以为还在远方的人
scene: 生日那天，灯一直关着，门后躲着一屋子的朋友，她一进门就叫出了声。 Her visit was completely unexpected.
sceneCN: 这里 unexpected 是「意外的」（第 1 个义项：事先没有想到）；句意为她来访完全出乎意料。推门见人的画面就是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「意外地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「意外性」
去掉否定前缀与原后缀的动词，义为「期待；预料」
动词加 -ation 构成名词，义为「期待；预期」

senses.title: Not what anyone thought would happen
senses.definition: not believed likely to happen, so that it takes people by surprise
senses.definitionCN: 被认为不太会发生，因而让人吃惊
senses.example: Her answer was so unexpected that no one spoke for a while.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答太出人意料，一时间谁都没说话。
senses.why: The prefix removes the verb of looking forward, so what is not looked forward to arrives without warning.
senses.whyCN: 前缀去掉了「向前张望」这个动作，没被张望的事物就毫无预告地到来了。

senses.title: A visit or arrival nobody planned for
senses.definition: used of a guest or arrival that no one had prepared for
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有人做过准备的客人或到来
senses.example: An unexpected visitor knocked just as dinner was served.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭刚端上桌，一位不速之客敲了门。
senses.why: The most visible kind of the unlooked-for is a person at the door.
senses.whyCN: 没被预料的种种事物中，最显眼的就是站在门口的那个人。

senses.title: An outcome that differs from the forecast
senses.definition: used of a result, turn, or ending that no one predicted
senses.definitionCN: 形容没人预测到的结果、转折或结局
senses.example: The trial took an unexpected turn on the second day.
senses.exampleCN: 审判第二天出现了意外的转折。
senses.why: Expect also means to predict, so a result that escapes prediction is unexpected.
senses.whyCN: expect 也有「预测」之义，逃出预测的结果自然就是意外的。

senses.title: Sudden in a slightly awkward way
senses.definition: happening at a moment that feels awkward or poorly timed
senses.definitionCN: 发生在让人觉得尴尬或不合适的时候
senses.example: An unexpected silence made the joke fall flat.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵突兀的沉默让那个笑话落了空。
senses.why: Surprise and discomfort are neighbours, so the word often carries a hint of awkwardness.
senses.whyCN: 惊讶与不适本是邻居，因此这个词常常带着一点尴尬的意味。

senses.title: Costs that were not budgeted for
senses.definition: used of money that must be spent beyond what was planned
senses.definitionCN: 形容超出原计划必须支出的钱款
senses.example: Unexpected repairs ate up the whole holiday fund.
senses.exampleCN: 预算外的修理费吃掉了整笔度假基金。
senses.why: Whatever was not planned for will also not be budgeted for.
senses.whyCN: 凡是没被计划在内的，也就没被编进预算。

intro.en: Expect comes from Latin through French, and the negative adjective was formed in English.
intro.cn: expect 经由法语来自拉丁语，带否定前缀的形容词则是英语自己造出来的。

items.en: Exspectare meant to look out for, from ex-, out, and spectare, to look.
items.cn: exspectare 意为「向外张望」，由 ex-（向外）与 spectare（看）构成。

items.en: The verb passed into French as expecter, keeping the sense of awaiting.
items.cn: 这个动词进入法语作 expecter，保留「等候」之义。

items.en: English borrowed it as expect and used it for awaiting something with confidence.
items.cn: 英语借入作 expect，用来表示有把握地等候某事。

items.en: The sense widened to predicting or supposing what will happen.
items.cn: 其意义扩展为预测或设想将会发生的事。

items.en: Un- placed before the past participle gave a word for what nobody looked for.
items.cn: 在过去分词前加 un-，就得到了表示「没人张望过之事」的词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the expect family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 expect 词族，近义组汇集表示惊讶的词。

entries.definition: to think that something will happen
in a way nobody planned for
a belief that something will happen
not changed or influenced
entries.definitionCN: 未受影响的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: causing surprise
happening very quickly
not known in advance
known in advance to be coming

normalIntro.en: The word is a looking-forward verb with the looking taken away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是「向前张望」的动词，把张望拿走了。

normal.en: Un- plus expected: not looked forward to.
normal.cn: un- 加 expected：没被张望过的。

normal.en: Expect comes from spectare, to look, which is also in spectator.
normal.cn: expect 源自 spectare（看），spectator 里也有这个词根。

normal.en: Unexpectedly is the adverb that usually sits next to arrive or happen.
normal.cn: unexpectedly 这个副词常跟在 arrive 或 happen 旁边。

normal.en: Completely unexpected is a very common intensifier pattern.
normal.cn: completely unexpected 是很常见的加强说法。

normal.en: Unexpected expenses and unexpected guests are two familiar collocations.
normal.cn: unexpected expenses 与 unexpected guests 是两个熟悉的搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a door swinging open to a room full of friends.
abstract.cn: 想象门一推开，屋里站满朋友。

abstract.en: See a test paper turned over with a question you never revised.
abstract.cn: 看一张翻过来的试卷，上面有一道从没复习的题。

abstract.en: Feel the half-second before the brain catches up with the eyes.
abstract.cn: 体会眼睛看到、脑子还没跟上之前的那半秒。

examples.en: Her arrival at the party was completely unexpected.
examples.cn: 她出现在聚会上，完全出乎大家的意料。

examples.en: An unexpected letter changed his plans for the year.
examples.cn: 一封意外的来信改变了他这一年的计划。

examples.en: Unexpectedly, the old machine started again on its own.
examples.cn: 出乎意料的是，那台旧机器又自己转了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺一看是个屁的」——推门一看根本不是那人，白等一场，真是意外。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ expected，expect 源自拉丁语 exspectare（向外张望），由 ex-（向外）+ spectare（看）构成

sensesIntro.en: One negation of looking ahead spreads to visitors, results, moments, and bills.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对「提前张望」的否定，蔓延到访客、结果、时刻与账单上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened to someone you did not know was coming.
core.cn: 核心意象：推开门看见一个你不知道会来的人。

branches.en: The core branch: what was not looked forward to at all.
branches.cn: 核心分支：完全没有被提前张望的事。

branches.en: The arrival branch: the person at the door.
branches.cn: 到来分支：门口站着的那个人。

branches.en: The result branch: an outcome nobody predicted.
branches.cn: 结果分支：没人预测到的结局。

branches.en: The timing branch: the moment that makes people wince.
branches.cn: 时机分支：让人尴尬的那个时刻。

branches.en: The money branch: the bill that was never planned.
branches.cn: 金钱分支：从未计划过的支出。

intro.en: The parts are an English prefix and a Latin-looking verb, all transparent in spelling.
intro.cn: 部件是英语前缀和一个带拉丁血统的动词，拼写上一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The looking root spectare also yields spectacle, spectator, and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「看」的词根 spectare 还生出 spectacle、spectator 与 inspect。

items.example: Spectare is the root of spectacle.
items.exampleCN: spectare 是 spectacle 的词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词后缀

items.example: An unforeseen delay cost them the train.
items.exampleCN: 一次未能预见的耽误让他们错过了火车。

definition_en: a person who works on a ship; a person who sails boats for sport
core_image: 一个站在甲板上、手里拉着缆绳的水手
scene: 老水手讲起了海上的故事。 The old sailor told stories of the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sailor 是「水手、海员」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老水手讲起了海上的故事。

senses.title: A ship worker
senses.definition: a person who works on a ship or boat
senses.definitionCN: 在轮船或小船上工作的人
senses.example: The sailor tied the ropes tightly.
senses.exampleCN: 水手把绳子系得很紧。
senses.why: The core sense is a person who works with sails and ships.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是与帆和船一起工作的人。

senses.title: A sailing sportsperson
senses.definition: a person who sails boats for sport
senses.definitionCN: 为运动而驾驶帆船的人
senses.example: She is a skilled sailor in small boats.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一名熟练的小帆船运动员。
senses.why: Work on ships becomes sport on water.
senses.whyCN: 船上的工作变成水上运动。

senses.title: An experienced voyager
senses.definition: a person who is experienced in travelling by sea
senses.definitionCN: 有丰富海上旅行经验的人
senses.example: The old sailor knew every star.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老航海者认识每一颗星。
senses.why: Skill with boats becomes knowledge of the sea.
senses.whyCN: 驾船技能变成对海洋的了解。

intro.en: Sailor is sail plus the person ending -or, meaning one who sails.
intro.cn: sailor 由 sail 加表示人的词尾 -or 构成，意为「驾船的人」。

items.en: Segl names the cloth that catches wind.
items.cn: segl 指兜风的布。

items.en: The ending -or marks a person who does something.
items.cn: 词尾 -or 标记从事某事的人。

items.en: Sailor names a person who sails.
items.cn: sailor 指驾船航行的人。

items.en: Sailor also names a sailing sportsperson.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sailor 也指帆船运动员。

items.en: Sail, sailing, and sailboat share the same base.
items.cn: sail、sailing 与 sailboat 共享同一词基。

note.en: Sailor works on a ship; tailor makes clothes.
note.cn: sailor 是在船上工作的人，tailor 则是裁缝。

a man who is not married
a ship that sails well

a sailor

normalIntro.en: A sailor is a person whose work or sport is sailing.
normalIntro.cn: sailor 是以航行作为工作或运动的人。

normal.en: The sailor climbed the mast.
normal.cn: 水手爬上了桅杆。

normal.en: Sailors learn to tie many knots.
normal.cn: 水手要学会打很多种结。

normal.en: The young sailor missed his family.
normal.cn: 年轻的水手想念家人。

normal.en: She became a sailor at eighteen.
normal.cn: 她十八岁成为水手。

normal.en: The sailor watched the horizon.
normal.cn: 水手望着地平线。

abstract.en: Picture a figure on deck pulling a rope.
abstract.cn: 想象甲板上拉绳子的身影。

abstract.en: Imagine a face weathered by salt and wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被盐和风磨砺的脸。

abstract.en: Think of a person who reads the sea like a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一个把大海当地图来读的人。

examples.en: The sailors worked through the night.
examples.cn: 水手们工作了一整夜。

examples.en: He is a sailor in the navy.
examples.cn: 他是海军水兵。

examples.en: The sailor knew the stars well.
examples.cn: 这位航海者很熟悉星辰。

dict_mnemonic.text: sail 加表示人的后缀 -or：驾船航行的人，就是 sailor（水手）。

root: 由 sail 加表示人的词尾 -or 构成，核心义「以驾船航行为职或为乐的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Sailor means a person who works on a ship, sails for sport, or is experienced at sea.
sensesIntro.cn: sailor 意为在船上工作的人、帆船运动员，或有海上经验的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure on deck holding a rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：甲板上握着缆绳的身影。

branches.en: The base sense is a person who works on ships.
branches.cn: 基础义是在船上工作的人。

branches.en: Ship work becomes water sport.
branches.cn: 船上工作变成水上运动。

branches.en: Boat skill becomes knowledge of the sea.
branches.cn: 驾船技能变成对海洋的了解。

branches.en: Professional and sporting sailors share the same skill.
branches.cn: 职业水手与运动水手共享同一种技能。

branches.en: Working on ships and knowing the sea go together.
branches.cn: 在船上工作与了解海洋相互关联。

intro.en: Sailor is sail plus -or, and it sits at the center of the sail word family.
intro.cn: sailor 由 sail 加 -or 构成，处于 sail 词族的中心。

latinIntro.en: Sailor has no Latin root; both parts are English.

definition_en: the highest point of a mountain, or a meeting of leaders
core_image: 登山者站在雪线之上的山巅，云在脚下
scene: 他们在天亮前到达了山顶。 They reached the summit before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 summit 是「山顶」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在天亮前到达了山顶。

senses.title: The top of a mountain
senses.definition: the highest point of a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 山的最高的地方
senses.example: They reached the summit before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在天亮前到达了山顶。
senses.why: This is the concrete physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是具体的物理义项。

senses.title: A meeting of leaders
senses.definition: a meeting between heads of governments
senses.definitionCN: 政府首脑之间的会议
senses.example: The two leaders met at a summit.
senses.exampleCN: 两位领导人在一次峰会上会面。
senses.why: The word borrows the image of the top.
senses.whyCN: 这个词借用了「顶端」的意象。

senses.title: The highest point of something
senses.definition: the highest level of a career or process
senses.definitionCN: 事业或过程的最高阶段
senses.example: She is at the summit of her career.
senses.exampleCN: 她正处于事业的顶点。
senses.why: Here the image becomes abstract.
senses.whyCN: 这里意象变得抽象。

intro.en: Summit comes from Latin summus, the highest, through French sommet.
intro.cn: summit 来自拉丁语 summus（最高的），经法语 sommet 进入英语。

items.en: Summus meant highest.
items.cn: summus 意为最高的。

items.en: Sommet meant the top of a hill.
items.cn: sommet 意为小山顶。

items.en: Summet meant the highest point.
items.cn: summet 意为最高点。

items.en: Summit named a mountain top.
items.cn: summit 指山顶。

items.en: It extended to meetings of leaders.
items.cn: 它又扩展到领导人会议。

note.en: Summit is compared with look-alike words and with words for the top.
note.cn: 把 summit 与形近词以及表示顶点的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Summit is the highest point, where the mountain meets the sky.
normalIntro.cn: summit 是最高点，是山与天空相接的地方。

abstract.en: A summit is a place with nowhere higher to go.
abstract.cn: 顶峰是一个再没有更高处可去的地方。

abstract.en: Every summit is also a beginning of the descent.
abstract.cn: 每个顶峰也都是下山的开始。

abstract.en: Leaders climb to summits to see farther.
abstract.cn: 领导人登上峰会，是为了看得更远。

dict_mnemonic.text: summit 与 sum（总数）同出拉丁语 summus（最高的），本指山顶，又引申为最高级别的峰会与事业的顶点。

root: 来自拉丁语 summus（最高的），经古法语 sommet（山顶）进入英语，由山顶引申为峰会与顶点。

sensesIntro.en: Summit means the top of a mountain, a meeting of leaders, or the highest point of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: summit 表示山顶、领导人峰会，或任何事物的最高点。

core.en: The highest point, physical or not.
core.cn: 最高点，无论具体还是抽象。

definition_zh: 振动；震颤；（声音）回荡；颤动
definition_en: to move quickly and slightly to and fro, or to sound with a shaking tone
core_image: 手机静音放在桌面，屏幕亮起前桌子轻轻嗡了一下
scene: 车到站时，地板先轻微一颤，行李箱的拉杆跟着抖。 The floor vibrated as the train pulled into the station.
sceneCN: 这里 vibrate 是「振动」（第 1 个义项：快速而轻微地来回运动）；句意为列车进站时地板在振动。桌上手机嗡一下的那种轻颤就是这个动作的意思。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「振动；颤动」
现在分词作形容词，义为「震动的；颤动的」
加后缀 -atory 构成，义为「振动的」

senses.title: To shake quickly and slightly
senses.definition: to move back and forth very fast and with a small range
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的幅度快速来回运动
senses.example: The floor vibrated as the train pulled into the station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车进站时地板在震动。
senses.why: Latin vibrare described a swift, small shake, and that is still the core motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vibrare 指的正是快速而小幅的抖动，这仍是核心动作。

senses.title: To sound with a shaking tone
senses.definition: to produce or carry a sound that keeps shaking in the air
senses.definitionCN: 发出或在空气中持续震荡的声音
senses.example: His voice vibrated with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音因愤怒而发颤。
senses.why: A struck string shakes the air, and the shaking is what we hear as a living tone.
senses.whyCN: 被拨动的弦使空气震动，我们听到的那种「活」的音色就是这种震动。

senses.title: To be full of a strong feeling
senses.definition: to seem to shake with excitement, energy, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因兴奋、活力或情绪而显得震动
senses.example: The hall vibrated with applause.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里掌声雷动。
senses.why: When a crowded room shakes with sound, the place itself seems to tremble.
senses.whyCN: 满场的声音让整个空间都在震，地方本身也仿佛在颤。

senses.title: Of a machine, to work with a hum
senses.definition: to run with a steady small shaking, as an engine does
senses.definitionCN: 如发动机那样带着持续的小幅震动运转
senses.example: The old fridge vibrates all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧冰箱整夜嗡嗡作响。
senses.why: Machines turned the natural shake of matter into a daily background noise.
senses.whyCN: 机器把物质固有的抖动变成了日常的背景噪音。

senses.title: To swing between two choices
senses.definition: to move quickly between two states, as a mind between choices
senses.definitionCN: 像心思在两种选择间快速来回
senses.example: He vibrated between hope and fear.
senses.exampleCN: 他在希望与恐惧之间摇摆。
senses.why: A movement to and fro can describe a mind as easily as a string.
senses.whyCN: 来回摆动既可以形容琴弦，也可以形容心思。

intro.en: Vibrate comes from Latin vibrare, to shake or brandish, a motion small and fast.
intro.cn: vibrate 来自拉丁语 vibrare（抖动、挥舞），指的是一种小而快的运动。

items.en: Vibrare meant to shake, to quiver, and also to wave a weapon.
items.cn: vibrare 意为抖动、颤动，也表示挥舞武器。

items.en: The noun vibratio described a quivering movement.
items.cn: 名词 vibratio 描述颤动的运动。

items.en: English took vibrate in the seventeenth century, first for shaking bodies.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 vibrate，最初用于物体的抖动。

items.en: Sound and engines gave the word its everyday modern senses.
items.cn: 声音与发动机赋予它现代日常的含义。

items.en: Phones added the sense of a silent buzz in the pocket.
items.cn: 手机又添上口袋里无声的一阵嗡动。

note.en: The first group holds the vibration family, the second the nearby verbs of shaking and steadying.
note.cn: 第一组是 vibration 词族，第二组是表示晃动与稳定的相近动词。

full of energy and colour
a shaking in a sung note

to shake from fear or cold

normalIntro.en: A slip of -ate on the Latin stem vibr- gives a verb for any fast, small shake.
normalIntro.cn: 在拉丁词干 vibr- 上加 -ate，就得到表示任何快速小抖动的动词。

normal.en: Vibrate, vibration, vibrant all share the Latin stem vibr-.
normal.cn: vibrate、vibration、vibrant 共有拉丁词干 vibr-。

normal.en: A string, a floor, a phone: the smaller the shake, the better the word.
normal.cn: 琴弦、地板、手机：抖得越小，越适合这个词。

normal.en: British stress falls on the second syllable, American often on the first.
normal.cn: 英式重音在第二音节，美式常在第一音节。

normal.en: Keep the final -e before -ion: vibration.
normal.cn: 加 -ion 前保留词尾 -e：vibration。

normal.en: Old Latin vibrare also meant to brandish a spear.
normal.cn: 古拉丁语 vibrare 还表示挥舞长矛。

abstract.en: Feel a phoned handset humming on a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 感受桌上的手机在震。

abstract.en: See a violin string after the bow has left it.
abstract.cn: 想琴弓离开后仍在颤的琴弦。

abstract.en: Hear a whole hall shaking with clapping.
abstract.cn: 听整个大厅被掌声震得发响。

examples.en: The windows vibrated whenever a truck went past.
examples.cn: 每当有卡车经过，窗户就震动。

examples.en: Her voice vibrated with excitement on the phone.
examples.cn: 电话里她的声音因兴奋而发颤。

examples.en: Set the phone to vibrate during the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会时把手机调成振动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪不瑞特」——歪着的架子不稳，一碰就抖个不停。

root: 拉丁语 vibrare（抖动；挥舞）→ vibratio（颤动）→ 英语 vibrate

sensesIntro.en: One verb of tiny fast motion grows into sound, into a crowded hall, into engines, and finally into a wavering mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示极快小幅运动的动词，长成声音、长成满场掌声、长成机器嗡鸣，最后长成摇摆不定的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone buzzing on a wooden table.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桌上嗡动的手机。

branches.en: The motion branch: a floor shaking as the train arrives.
branches.cn: 运动分支：列车进站时震动的车厢地板。

branches.en: The sound branch: a voice shaking with anger.
branches.cn: 声音分支：因愤怒而颤抖的声音。

branches.en: The crowd branch: a hall trembling with applause.
branches.cn: 人群分支：被掌声震动的大厅。

branches.en: The machine branch: the fridge humming all night.
branches.cn: 机器分支：整夜嗡鸣的冰箱。

branches.en: The mind branch: swinging between hope and fear.
branches.cn: 心思分支：在希望与恐惧间摇摆。

intro.en: The Latin stem vibr- means to shake; -ate, -ion, and -ant build verb and nouns from it.
intro.cn: 拉丁词干 vibr- 意为抖动，-ate、-ion、-ant 由它构成动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vibrare yielded English vibrate, vibration, and vibrant, all keeping the small quick shake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vibrare 派生英语 vibrate、vibration、vibrant，都保留了小而快的抖动。

Vibrant means alive with quick energy.

definition_zh: 轨道；绕行；（影响、势力）范围；眼窝；原子轨道
definition_en: the curved path of one body around another, or to move along such a path
core_image: 孩子甩着一根系绳的小球，小球绕着握绳的手一圈圈转，绳在空气里拉出圆的痕迹
scene: 操场边的孩子把一只系绳的小球甩起来，小球绕着握绳的手一圈圈转。 The child lets the ball swing in a wide orbit around one hand.
sceneCN: 这里 orbit 指「一个物体绕另一个物体运行的路径」（第 1 个义项：绕行的曲线路径）；句意为孩子让小球绕着一只手划出宽宽的轨道。图中可辨识物件：系绳小球、握绳的手、圆形痕迹、操场地面、孩子背影；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 轨道；势力范围；眼窝；（物理）原子轨道

senses.title: A path around a body
senses.definition: the curved path of a body around a more massive one under gravity
senses.definitionCN: 在引力作用下，一个天体绕更大质量天体的弯曲路径
senses.example: The child lets the ball swing in a wide orbit around one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子让小球绕着一只手划出宽宽的轨道。
senses.why: the word began as the rut of a wheel, so the earliest idea is a track that something follows rather than a force that pulls it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指车轮的辙，因此最早的想法是某物沿着走的轨迹，而非拉着它的力。

senses.title: To move along that path
senses.definition: to travel around a body in a closed or repeating path
senses.definitionCN: 沿闭合或重复的路径绕某天体运行
senses.example: The station orbits the earth once every ninety minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 空间站每九十分钟绕地球一圈。
senses.why: once the noun meant a track, the verb could mean travelling on it, and English formed it without adding any new root.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词意为轨迹，动词自然可意为沿轨迹行进，英语无需另加词根就构成了它。

senses.title: One complete circuit
senses.definition: one completed trip around a body, used as a unit of time or counting
senses.definitionCN: 绕某天体完整走完的一圈，用作计时或计数的单位
senses.example: The satellite completed its thousandth orbit this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗卫星今早完成了第千圈绕行。
senses.why: a closed path can be counted, so the same noun measures repetition rather than only geometry.
senses.whyCN: 闭合路径可以计数，因此同一个名词也度量重复次数，而不只度量几何。

senses.title: An electron's orbital
senses.titleCN: 物理与化学中的原子轨道
senses.definition: in physics and chemistry, a region where an electron is likely to be found around a nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 物理与化学中指电子在核周围出现的概率区域
senses.example: The first shell holds one spherical orbital.
senses.exampleCN: 第一层只有一个球形轨道。
senses.why: early models pictured electrons circling like planets, and the word survived after the picture became a probability cloud.
senses.whyCN: 早期模型把电子想成像行星一样绕行，而在这个图像变成概率云之后，这个词仍留了下来。

senses.title: The eye socket
senses.definition: the bony cavity that holds the eye
senses.definitionCN: 容纳眼球的骨质腔
senses.example: A blow near the orbit can damage the eye itself.
senses.exampleCN: 眼窝附近的打击可能伤到眼睛本身。
senses.why: the socket is a ring-shaped hollow, and Latin used the same wheel-track word for it, so English kept both senses.
senses.whyCN: 眼窝是环形的凹处，拉丁语用同一个「车辙」词指它，因此英语保留了两义。

senses.title: A sphere of influence
senses.definition: the range within which a person, country or idea exerts influence
senses.definitionCN: 一个人、国家或观念施加影响的范围
senses.example: Smaller states moved into the larger neighbour's orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 较小的国家进入了更大邻国的影响圈。
senses.why: bodies near a massive one are held by it, so politics borrowed the picture for clients held by a power.
senses.whyCN: 靠近大质量天体的物体会被它牵住，因此政治借这幅图景指被某个强国牵住的附庸。

senses.title: Going into orbit
senses.definition: used of spacecraft reaching and staying in a path around a body
senses.definitionCN: 指航天器抵达并停留在绕某天体的路径上
senses.example: The rocket put the weather satellite into orbit within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭在一小时内把气象卫星送入轨道。
senses.why: spaceflight made the phrase everyday, and 'into orbit' became a fixed way to describe a successful launch.
senses.whyCN: 航天让这个短语变得日常，「进入轨道」成了描述发射成功的固定说法。

senses.title: Going round the same subject
senses.titleCN: 比喻：绕着同一个问题打转
senses.definition: figuratively, to keep returning to one topic without settling it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻反复回到同一个话题却始终不解决
senses.example: The meeting orbited the budget question for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会议绕着预算问题转了整整两小时。
senses.why: an orbit returns to the same point, so the metaphor describes discussion that moves but never arrives.
senses.whyCN: 轨道会回到同一点，因此这个比喻形容讨论在动却始终不到达。

senses.title: Named orbital regimes
senses.titleCN: 按高度命名的轨道类型
senses.definition: used in fixed names such as low Earth orbit, polar orbit and geostationary orbit
senses.definitionCN: 用于近地轨道、极轨道、地球静止轨道等固定名称
senses.example: Most communication satellites sit in geostationary orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 多数通信卫星位于地球静止轨道。
senses.why: each regime has different uses, so the noun became part of technical labels that say where a satellite works.
senses.whyCN: 各轨道区间用途不同，因此这个名词成为说明卫星工作位置的技术标签的一部分。

intro.en: Orbit comes from Latin orbita 'wheel-rut, track', from orbis 'circle, disk'. English first used it for the eye socket and only later for a heavenly path. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: orbit 来自拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」，其源为 orbis「圆、盘」。英语最早用它指眼窝，后来才指天体路径。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita was the rut a wheel leaves, and by extension any beaten track or course.
items.cn: orbita 是车轮留下的辙，引申为任何被踩出的轨迹或行程。

items.en: Orbis meant a circle, a disk or the round world; the track word was built from it.
items.cn: orbis 意为圆、盘或圆形的世界；轨迹一词即由它构成。

items.en: English orbit first named the bony ring around the eye, a sense Latin already had.
items.cn: 英语 orbit 最早指眼周的骨环，这一义拉丁语已有。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy applied the same word to the path of a body, since both are enclosing tracks.
items.cn: 17 世纪天文学把同一个词用于天体路径，因为两者都是围合的轨迹。

items.en: The twentieth century made 'into orbit' a household phrase and added named regimes such as low Earth orbit.
items.cn: 20 世纪使「进入轨道」成为家常用语，并增添了近地轨道等命名区间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of orbis is not established, and any older Indo-European form suggested for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：orbis 在拉丁语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the derived forms that are easily swapped; group two holds words for a route or a turn.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混用的派生形式；第二组是表示路线或一圈的词。

entries.definition: Of an orbit, or in chemistry a noun for an electron's probability region.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道的；化学中也作名词指电子的概率区域。

entries.definition: The present participle, used for something currently in orbit rather than for the path itself.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，指当前正在轨运行的事物，而非路径本身。

entries.definition: A spacecraft designed to circle a body; the -er suffix marks the agent, not the path.
entries.definitionCN: 设计用来绕某天体飞行的航天器；-er 后缀标记执行者，而非路径。

entries.definition: A sphere or globe, from the same orbis; it names the round thing, not the track around it.
entries.definitionCN: 球体或圆球，同出 orbis；它命名圆的东西，而非绕它的轨迹。

entries.definition: The path of a moving body, often one that does not repeat; an orbit is the repeating case.
entries.definitionCN: 运动天体的路径，常指不重复者；轨道是其中重复的情形。

entries.definition: A single circling; it names the motion, while orbit names the track.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行一圈；它命名运动，而 orbit 命名轨迹。

entries.definition: A perfectly round curve; orbits are usually ellipses, so circle is only the special case.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的圆形曲线；轨道通常是椭圆，圆只是特例。

entries.definition: The extent something can reach; it overlaps the 'sphere of influence' sense but has no orbital image.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所能达到的范围；与「势力范围」义重叠，但没有轨道意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relations, real compounds and real etymology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词族关系、真实搭配与真实词源，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin orbita 'wheel-rut': the path is a groove in space.
normal.cn: 拉丁 orbita「车辙」：路径是空间中磨出的沟。

normal.en: English used orbit for the eye socket before it used it for the moon.
normal.cn: 英语先用 orbit 指眼窝，后来才用它指月球。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbital, orbiting, orbiter, orbit insertion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbital、orbiting、orbiter、orbit insertion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark spaceflight: go into orbit, low Earth orbit, geostationary orbit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标记航天：进入轨道、近地轨道、地球静止轨道。

normal.en: The electron sense survives in chemistry as the orbital.
normal.cn: 电子义在化学中以 orbital 的形式留存。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that keeps circling a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话老绕着一扇锁着的门打转。

abstract.en: Picture a small country held in the gravity of a large one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小国被大国的引力牵住。

abstract.en: Picture a stone skipping around a whirlpool instead of falling in.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子绕着旋涡转，而没有掉进去。

examples.en: The moon's orbit is tilted about five degrees from the ecliptic.
examples.cn: 月球轨道相对黄道倾斜约五度。

examples.en: Engineers raised the satellite's orbit to extend its life.
examples.cn: 工程师抬高了卫星轨道以延长其寿命。

examples.en: The discussion orbited the same objection all afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午的讨论都绕着同一个反对意见打转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，比它（orbit）」——哦，它又比它多绕了一圈 → 轨道、绕行

root: 拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」← orbis「圆、盘」；英语先指眼窝，17 世纪起指天体路径。orbis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the track to the act of following it, to one turn, to an electron's cloud, an eye socket, a sphere of influence, a launch, a metaphor and named orbital zones.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从轨迹出发，到沿轨迹行进、一整圈、电子的云、眼窝、势力范围、一次发射、一个比喻，最后到按高度命名的轨道区间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a string, circling a hand and leaving a ring in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只系绳的小球绕手转，在空气里留下一圈痕迹。

branches.en: MOTION AND COUNT: travelling on the path, and one completed lap.
branches.cn: 运动与计数：沿路径行进，以及走完一圈。

branches.en: RINGS AT SMALL SCALE: electron clouds and eye sockets repeat the enclosing circle.
branches.cn: 小尺度的环：电子云与眼窝重复了围合的圆圈。

branches.en: HELD IN PLACE: politics and argument both describe bodies that cannot leave a centre.
branches.cn: 被牵在原处：政治与争论都描述离不开中心的东西。

branches.en: ENGINEERED ORBITS: launches and named regimes turn the path into a destination.
branches.cn: 被工程化的轨道：发射与命名区间把路径变成目的地。

branches.en: ROOT IMAGE: the wheel-rut is the whole family's source.
branches.cn: 根源意象：车辙是整个词族的来源。

intro.en: Orbit is a Latin noun with a small English family built by suffixes for relation, action and agent.
intro.cn: orbit 是一个拉丁名词，英语用表示关系、动作与执行者的后缀构建了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin orbita 'track' and orbis 'circle' supply orbit and orb; the family has no Greek element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 orbita「轨迹」与 orbis「圆」提供 orbit 与 orb；这个词族不含希腊成分。

items.example: The Latin word is the direct source of orbit.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词是 orbit 的直接来源。

items.example: The probe orbited the planet for a year.
items.exampleCN: 探测器绕这颗行星运行了一年。
一座在轨实验室从头顶经过。

items.example: The orbiter mapped the surface for years.
items.exampleCN: 轨道飞行器测绘地表多年。

latinEntries.structure: orbis terrarum (noun phrase, third declension + genitive plural)
latinEntries.meaning: the circle of lands, the whole world

definition_en: a strong feeling of sympathy for someone who is suffering, together with a wish to help
core_image: 看见别人蹲在雨里发抖，自己也不由得停下脚步
scene: 同事的母亲住院，她把热汤放在对方桌上没有多问。 Her compassion showed in small, quiet acts.
sceneCN: 这里 compassion 指「同情；关怀」（第 1 个义项：对他人苦难的体恤）；句意是她的关怀体现在细小而安静的举动里。

senses.title: Sympathy for suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of pity for someone who is suffering
senses.definitionCN: 对正在受苦之人的怜惜之情
senses.example: She felt deep compassion for the lost child.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个走失的孩子深感同情。
senses.why: Com- means with, and the root means to suffer, so compassion is suffering alongside.
senses.whyCN: com- 表示与…同在，词根表示受苦，所以 compassion 是与他人一同受苦。

senses.title: Sympathy that moves you to help
senses.definition: sympathy strong enough to make you want to act
senses.definitionCN: 强到让你想要行动的同情
senses.example: The nurse treated every patient with compassion.
senses.exampleCN: 这位护士以关怀之心对待每位病人。
senses.why: Feeling alone is passive; compassion carries the push to ease another's pain.
senses.whyCN: 单纯的感觉是被动的，compassion 带着减轻他人痛苦的推力。

intro.en: Compassion comes from Latin com, with, and pati, to suffer: to feel pain together with someone.
intro.cn: compassion 来自拉丁语 com（与…同在）与 pati（受苦）：与某人一同感到疼痛。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer or to endure.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦或忍受。

items.en: Compassio meant suffering together with another person.
items.cn: compassio 意为与另一个人一同受苦。

items.en: The church used compassio for shared grief.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语教会用 compassio 指共同承担的悲伤。

items.en: Old French compassion softened it into tender pity.
items.cn: 古法语 compassion 把它软化为温柔的怜惜。

items.en: English compassion joined pity with the wish to help.
items.cn: 英语 compassion 把怜惜与想帮忙的心愿合在一起。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the spelling of compassion, and the meaning group separates sympathy, pity and empathy.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写与 compassion 相近的词，近义组分辨同情、怜悯与共情。

entries.definition: showing kindness to people who suffer
a very strong feeling
able to work well together
the feeling of being sorry for someone
sorrow for the bad luck of another
the ability to share another person's feelings

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with shared suffering, then move to the push to help and to the quiet shape it takes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从共同受苦开始，再走到想帮忙的推力以及它安静的样子。

normal.en: Com- is with and passion here means suffering, so compassion is feeling with someone.
normal.cn: com- 是与…同在，这里的 passion 指受苦，所以 compassion 就是与人同感。

normal.en: Pity looks down; compassion sits down beside you.
normal.cn: pity 是俯视，compassion 是在你身边坐下。

normal.en: Compassion is not softness; it often means doing the hard thing.
normal.cn: compassion 不是软弱，它常常意味着去做难做的事。

normal.en: The adjective is compassionate, the adverb compassionately.
normal.cn: 形容词是 compassionate，副词是 compassionately。

normal.en: Compassion fatigue is what carers feel after too many nights.
normal.cn: 同情疲劳是照护者熬过太多夜晚后的感受。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger holding an umbrella over someone already wet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人把伞举到已经淋湿的人头上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand placed quietly on a shaking shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手静静放在发抖的肩上。

abstract.en: Picture hot soup left on a desk with no note.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗热汤放在桌上，没有留字条。

examples.en: Her compassion for the stray dogs was well known.
examples.cn: 她对流浪狗的同情是出了名的。

examples.en: He spoke with compassion rather than blame.
examples.cn: 他说话带着同情，而不是责备。

examples.en: Compassion costs nothing but means everything.
examples.cn: 同情不花一文，却意义重大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compassion 记成 com（一起）加 passion（受苦）：与人一起受苦，就是同情。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 pati（受苦），本义是与他人一同受苦，后引申为同情、怜悯与愿意相助的关怀。

sensesIntro.en: From feeling another's pain, to being moved to relieve it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从感受他人的痛苦，到被推动去减轻它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stopping in the rain because a stranger is shivering.
core.cn: 核心意象：看见别人蹲在雨里发抖，自己也不由得停下脚步。

branches.en: Feeling the pain is the root sense of compassion.
branches.cn: 感受到那份痛，是 compassion 的词根义。

branches.en: Compassion that stays a feeling has not finished its work.
branches.cn: 只停在感受上的 compassion，还没有做完它的事。

branches.en: Feeling and acting are one movement in this word.
branches.cn: 在这个词里，感受与行动是同一个动作。

branches.en: The Latin root already joined the pain with the shared response.
branches.cn: 拉丁词根早已把痛与共同的回应连在一起。

branches.en: Care shows best in small acts that ask for no thanks.
branches.cn: 关怀最常显现在不讨谢意的小事上。

intro.en: Compassion is built on Latin com, with, plus the suffering base pati.
intro.cn: compassion 由拉丁语 com（与…同在）加表示受苦的词基 pati 构成。

latinIntro.en: The same patient root gives patient and patience, both about enduring.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个表示忍受的词根还给出 patient 与 patience，两者都与忍耐有关。

items.exampleCN: 有同情心的医生先倾听。

items.example: She spoke compassionately to the boy.
items.exampleCN: 她带着同情对男孩说话。

items.meaning: calm and not led by feeling
items.exampleCN: 法官必须保持冷静客观。
他冷静地评判了这个案子。

items.meaning: tiredness from caring for too long
items.exampleCN: 护士常受同情疲劳之苦。
失败之后，自我关怀有帮助。

definition_en: a compound used in cooking and cleaning, a sweet fizzy drink, or carbonated water
core_image: 玻璃杯里冒着气泡的冷饮
scene: 他点了一杯加冰的汽水。 He ordered a soda with ice.
sceneCN: 这里 soda 是「汽水」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他点了一杯加冰的汽水。

senses.title: Soda compound
senses.definition: a white compound used in cooking, cleaning, and industry
senses.definitionCN: 用于烹饪、清洁和工业的白色化合物
senses.example: Add a spoon of baking soda to the flour.
senses.exampleCN: 往面粉里加一勺小苏打。
senses.why: This is the chemical sense behind the name.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词背后的化学义项。

senses.title: Fizzy drink
senses.definition: a sweet drink made with carbonated water
senses.definitionCN: 用碳酸水制成的甜味饮料
senses.example: He ordered a soda with ice.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯加冰的汽水。
senses.why: Everyday use names a sweet soft drink.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法指甜的软饮料。

senses.title: Carbonated water
senses.definition: water charged with gas and often used in mixed drinks
senses.definitionCN: 充入气体、常用于调配饮料的水
senses.example: She drinks soda water with lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她喝加柠檬的苏打水。
senses.why: The word also names the plain fizzy water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指不加糖的气泡水。

intro.en: Soda came through Italian and medieval Latin from an Arabic word for a salt plant.
intro.cn: soda 经意大利语和中世纪拉丁语来自阿拉伯语中表示盐生植物的词。

items.en: Soda named a salt-rich plant used for cleaning.
items.cn: soda 指一种富含盐分、用于清洁的植物。

items.en: The word named the compound taken from that plant.
items.cn: 这个词指从该植物中取得的化合物。

items.en: English adopted soda for the white alkaline powder.
items.cn: 英语借入 soda，指白色碱性粉末。

items.en: Soda water brought the sense of fizzy water.
items.cn: soda water 带来了气泡水的意思。

items.en: American shops made soda a word for a sweet drink.
items.cn: 美国商店使 soda 成为甜味饮料的叫法。

note.en: Soda is compared with look-alike words and other drinks.
note.cn: 把 soda 与形近词以及其他饮料词作比较。

relating to the sun
to join metal with a melted alloy
a sweet fizzy drink in informal use
a fizzy drink often mixed with gin
water from a spring, often fizzy

normalIntro.cn: soda 从白色粉末开始，最后变成杯中的气泡。

normal.en: The old shop still has a soda fountain.
normal.cn: 那家老店仍有一个冷饮柜。

abstract.en: A small bubble can lift a whole drink.
abstract.cn: 一个小气泡能托起整杯饮料。

abstract.en: The same powder cleans a pan and raises bread.
abstract.cn: 同一种粉末既能清洁锅，也能让面包发起。

abstract.en: Ordinary things often hide a chemical story.
abstract.cn: 寻常之物常藏着化学的故事。

examples.en: He ordered a soda with ice.
examples.cn: 他点了一杯加冰的汽水。

examples.en: She drinks soda water with lemon.

dict_mnemonic.text: soda 与 sofa、solar 形近；baking soda 是「小苏打」，soda water 是「苏打水」，soda pop 是「汽水」。

root: 经意大利语和中世纪拉丁语来自阿拉伯语，原指富含盐分的盐生植物，后指苏打化合物及其饮料。

sensesIntro.en: Soda is a chemical compound, a sweet fizzy drink, or carbonated water.
sensesIntro.cn: soda 指一种化合物、甜味汽水，或苏打水。

core.en: A salt that ends up in bubbles.
core.cn: 最终化作气泡的一种盐。

branches.en: White powder helps bread rise.
branches.cn: 白色粉末帮助面包发起。

branches.en: A sweet drink fizzes in the glass.
branches.cn: 甜饮料在杯中冒泡。

branches.en: Plain fizzy water is served with lemon.
branches.cn: 原味气泡水配柠檬上桌。

branches.en: The powder and the drink share one name.
branches.cn: 粉末与饮料共用一个名称。

branches.en: Sweet and plain drinks both carry bubbles.
branches.cn: 甜味和原味饮料都带着气泡。

intro.en: Soda builds words for baking, drinks, and serving counters.
intro.cn: soda 构成表示烘焙、饮料和冷饮柜的词。

latinIntro.en: The word reached English through medieval Latin and Italian.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经中世纪拉丁语和意大利语进入英语。

items.example: Soda is kept in a labelled jar.
items.exampleCN: 苏打放在有标签的罐子里。

items.example: Baking soda makes the cake light.
Soda pop is sold in the park.
The soda fountain closed years ago.
items.exampleCN: 那个冷饮柜多年前就关门了。

items.example: He bought a can of soda.

latinEntries.example: Medieval soda named a plant rich in salt.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语的 soda 指一种富含盐分的植物。

definition_en: to put something briefly into liquid, or to go down and then up again
core_image: 一片面包被捏着边角，往热汤里按下去又提起来
scene: 他把面包掰开，捏着一角很快按进汤里。 She dipped her hand in the cold stream.
sceneCN: 这里 dipped 指「浸入」（第 1 个义项：短时间放进液体里）；句意是她把手浸进冰凉的小溪。

senses.title: To put in liquid briefly
senses.definition: to lower something into liquid for a short moment
senses.definitionCN: 把东西放进液体里很短一会儿
senses.example: She dipped her hand in the cold stream.
senses.exampleCN: 她把手浸进冰凉的小溪。
senses.why: The hand goes down and comes back before the water can hold it.
senses.whyCN: 手沉下去又提起来，水还没来得及留住它。

senses.title: To fall and rise again
senses.definition: to go down for a while, as a number or a path does
senses.definitionCN: 像数字或道路那样暂时往下走
senses.example: Sales dipped below last year's level.
senses.exampleCN: 销量降到了去年的水平以下。
senses.why: The line on the chart bends down, then finds its way back.
senses.whyCN: 图上的线往下一沉，随后又找回自己。

senses.title: A hollow in the ground
senses.definition: a place where the surface goes down and then up
senses.definitionCN: 表面先往下再往上的一处地方
senses.example: A small dip in the road holds water after rain.
senses.exampleCN: 路上一个小坑雨后积着水。
senses.why: The motion of dipping becomes a shape in the land.
senses.whyCN: 「往下一沉」的动作，变成了地面上的一个形状。

intro.en: Dip comes from Old English dyppan, a Germanic verb for putting something into water.
intro.cn: dip 来自古英语 dyppan，是日耳曼语中表示「把东西放进水里」的动词。

items.en: A root dup- linked dipping with depth.
items.cn: 词根 dup- 把「浸」与「深」连在一起。

items.en: Dyppan meant to baptise or to plunge something in.
items.cn: dyppan 指施洗，或把东西按进水里。

items.en: Dippen widened to any short plunge into liquid.
items.cn: dippen 扩展到任何短时间的入水。

items.en: The noun named a hollow and a short swim.
items.cn: 名词义开始指凹坑与短暂的游泳。

items.en: Dipping also describes numbers falling for a while.
items.cn: dip 还用来形容数字暂时下滑。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the d- and short vowel, while the meaning group covers plunging, soaking and sinking.
note.cn: 形近组共用短元音与 d 开头，近义组则覆盖猛插、浸泡与下沉。

entries.definition: reaching far down from the top
entries.definitionCN: 从顶部往下延伸很远的

entries.definition: a long-handled cup for scooping liquid
a continuing loud noise
to push suddenly and deeply into something
to cover completely with liquid
to go down slowly below a surface

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with bread pressed into soup and end with a shallow hollow holding rain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从按进汤里的面包开始，最后落到一个积着雨水的小坑。

normal.en: Dip and deep share a root: what you dip goes toward depth.
normal.cn: dip 与 deep 同根：浸下去，就是朝深处走。

normal.en: Dip in is quick; soak is long.
normal.cn: dip in 是快的一下，soak 是长时间泡。

normal.en: Take a dip means the whole body gets the treatment.
normal.cn: take a dip 是说整个人都进去泡一泡。

normal.en: A dip in sales is a hollow on a chart.
normal.cn: 销量的 dip，是图表上的一个凹口。

normal.en: Dip into a book, not through it.
normal.cn: dip into 一本书，是翻几页，不是读完。

abstract.en: Picture bread going under soup for one second.
abstract.cn: 想象面包在汤里沉了一秒。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifting dark liquid from a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子从罐里舀起深色的液体。

abstract.en: Picture a shallow hollow shining after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后的浅坑里亮着一小片水。

examples.en: He dipped a brush into the paint.
examples.cn: 他把刷子蘸进颜料里。

examples.en: Temperatures dipped below zero last night.
examples.cn: 昨夜气温降到了零度以下。

examples.en: There is a dip in the path just before the gate.
examples.cn: 门前的小路上有一处凹陷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dip 记成「低扑」：低下去一扑，蘸一下又起来。

root: 来自古英语 dyppan，出自日耳曼语词根 dup-，与 deep 同源，本义是把东西按进水里。后来泛指任何短促的浸蘸，又用来形容数字或道路先降后升，作名词则指地面的凹陷或短暂泡水。

sensesIntro.en: From a quick plunge of bread into soup, to a falling line, to the hollow that line leaves in the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 从面包在汤里的一沉，到一条下落的线，再到那条线在地面上留下的凹坑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one corner of bread pressed under soup and lifted out.
core.cn: 核心意象：面包的一角按进汤里，又被提起来。

chain: A LINE ON A CHART BENDS DOWN

branches.en: The first sense is the short plunge into liquid.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是往液体里的那一沉。

branches.en: The second sense moves the plunge onto numbers.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这一沉挪到数字上。

branches.en: The third sense freezes the motion into ground.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这个动作冻成了地面。

branches.en: Both describe a short fall and a return.
branches.cn: 两者都描述短暂的下落与回返。

branches.en: A dip in a figure and a dip in a road look the same on paper.
branches.cn: 数字的下滑与路面的凹陷，画在纸上一个样。

intro.en: Dip forms a small family of scoops, tools and underwater birds.
intro.cn: dip 长出一小族词，涉及勺具、工具与潜水的水鸟。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is native Germanic and related to deep.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词是本土日耳曼语，与 deep 同源。

items.example: Dip the cloth in warm water.

items.exampleCN: 反复蘸刷子会浪费颜料。

items.example: The road dips near the bridge.
He filled the dipper at the well.
items.exampleCN: 他在井边把长柄勺舀满。

items.meaning: a rod for checking oil level
items.example: Pull the dipstick and wipe it clean.
The antenna is a simple dipole.
items.exampleCN: 这根天线是简单的偶极。

items.example: The old term dipsomania is rarely used now.
items.exampleCN: 嗜酒狂这个旧说法如今少见了。

definition_zh: 倾斜；倾向于；使倾向于；斜坡
definition_en: to lean or slope away from the vertical, to tend toward an opinion or action, and, as a noun, a sloping surface
core_image: 一根原本笔直的电线杆被风推得微微歪向一边
scene: 山路边的电线杆被风推得歪了一点，麻绳从杆子斜着垂下去。 He is inclined to agree, though he wants to see the numbers first.
sceneCN: 这里 incline 是「倾向于」（第 2 个义项：心思往某个方向偏），句意是他倾向于同意，不过想先看看数字。画面里有山路、微微歪斜的电线杆和斜垂的麻绳。

pos.zh: 动词：倾斜、使倾斜；（使）倾向于

senses.title: To lean or slope
senses.definition: to lean away from an upright position, or to make something slope
senses.definitionCN: 离开直立的位置而偏斜，或使某物形成斜坡
senses.example: The old gate inclines slightly towards the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇旧门微微朝路边歪着。
senses.why: This is the physical sense, and the Latin root simply means to lean.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体性的义项，拉丁词根本来就是「倚、倾」的意思。

senses.title: To tend towards something
senses.definition: to have a tendency or a mild wish to think or act in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 有某种倾向，或轻微地想做某事、持某种看法
senses.example: I incline to the view that the plan is too costly.
senses.exampleCN: 我倾向于认为这个方案代价太高。
senses.why: The mind leans the way a body leans, so the same verb describes opinions and wishes.
senses.whyCN: 心也会像身体那样往一边靠，于是同一个动词也能说看法与意愿。

senses.title: A sloping surface
senses.definition: a slope, especially one on a road or a railway
senses.definitionCN: 斜坡，尤指道路或铁路上的一段坡面
senses.example: The truck struggled up the long incline.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车吃力地爬上那段长坡。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun and now names the thing that leans.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词后，直接指那个倾斜的东西本身。

intro.en: Incline goes back to a Latin verb for leaning, and the leaning of the head, the body, and the mind all use the same image.
intro.cn: incline 出自拉丁语中表示「倚靠」的动词，头、身体与心思的倾斜都用同一个意象。

items.en: Clinare meant to bend or lean, and it also lies behind the word climate, the slanted zone of the earth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clinare 意为「弯、倚」，词语 climate（地球倾斜的地带）也从它而来。

items.en: Inclinare added in and meant to lean towards or upon something.
items.cn: inclinare 加上 in，意为「朝某物倾靠过去」。

items.en: Inclinatio named a leaning, and it was already used for a leaning of the mind.
items.cn: 名词 inclinatio 指倾斜，当时已用来比喻心思的偏向。

items.en: Old French carried the verb as incliner, still used of bodies, roofs, and opinions.
items.cn: 古法语以 incliner 沿用这个动词，既说身体、屋顶，也说看法。

items.en: English took it as incline, and the noun sense of a slope appeared later along with railway language.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 incline，名词「斜坡」义则随铁路用语稍后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the clin family of leaning; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of tendency.
note.cn: 形近组收 clin「倾」这一族词；近义组收表示「倾向于」的动词。

entries.definition: To lean away and so to go down or refuse; the opposite direction of incline.
entries.definitionCN: 「下降、拒绝」，同一词根方向朝下，与 incline 相对。

entries.definition: To lean back in a chair or on a bed.
The noun partner, meaning a tendency or a slope.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指倾向或倾斜度。

entries.definition: To be likely to do or be something over time.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「往往、有……的趋势」，多指长期倾向。

entries.definition: To bend the body or a thing to one side.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「倚、靠」，指身体或物体偏向一侧。

entries.definition: To rise or fall at an angle, as ground does.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「倾斜」，多用于地面与地形。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the body's lean visible inside the mental senses of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子让「身体倾斜」的画面在词的心理义里保持可见。

normal.en: To be inclined to do something is to lean towards it without yet walking.
normal.cn: be inclined to do 某事后，就是朝它歪了歪身子，还没迈步。

normal.en: Incline and decline differ by one prefix: leaning in versus leaning away.
normal.cn: incline 与 decline 只差一个前缀：一个往里靠，一个往外倒。

normal.en: The noun an incline is simply the slope you walk up, from the same word.
normal.cn: 名词 an incline 就是你走上去的那段坡，还是同一个词。

normal.en: The root also gave climate, the slanted band of the earth where the sun falls.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出了 climate，即太阳斜照的那一段地球。

normal.en: Disinclined flips the wish: not leaning, not willing.
normal.cn: disinclined 把意愿翻了过来：不倾身，也就是不乐意。

abstract.en: Opinions arrive as small inclinations before they harden into beliefs.
abstract.cn: 看法最初只是轻微的倾斜，后来才硬成信念。

abstract.en: Railway engineers needed a word for a gentle slope, and they borrowed the leaning of the human body.
abstract.cn: 铁路工程师需要给缓坡找个词，于是借用了人身体的倾斜。

abstract.en: The word quietly denies certainty: to incline is not to decide.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄否认了确定：倾向于，并不等于已经决定。

examples.en: The path inclines sharply after the second bridge.
examples.cn: 过了第二座桥，小路陡然而上。

examples.en: I am inclined to trust her account of the evening.
examples.cn: 我倾向于相信她对那天晚上的说法。

examples.en: The cyclist stood up for the final incline.
examples.cn: 骑手在最后那段坡上站了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 向 + cline 倾——身子朝某边倾，就是「倾向于」

root: 拉丁语 inclinare「倾靠」（in + clinare「弯、倚」），经古法语 incliner 于中世纪英语时期进入英语；身体性的倾斜先引申为心思的倾向，铁路用语又派生名词「斜坡」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: leaning physically, tending in mind or wish, and a slope you can walk up.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：身体上的倾斜，心思或意愿上的倾向，以及可以走上去的斜坡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a telephone pole pushed a little off upright by the wind, with a rope hanging at the same angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被风吹得微微歪斜的电线杆，麻绳也按同一个角度垂着。

branches.en: THE BODY: the verb starts as a physical lean.
branches.cn: 身体线：这个动词起初就是身体的倾斜。

branches.en: THE MIND: opinions lean before they settle.
branches.cn: 心思线：看法在定下来之前，先倾斜一下。

branches.en: THE ROAD: the noun names the slope itself.
branches.cn: 道路线：名词直接指那段坡。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: be inclined to do leaves room for doubt.
branches.cn: 搭配线：be inclined to do 给怀疑留了余地。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: inclination covers both the wish and the angle.
branches.cn: 词族线：inclination 同时指意愿与倾斜度。

intro.en: The table gathers members of the clin family, where the root means to bend or lean.
intro.cn: 此表汇集 clin 一族词，其词根意为「弯、倚」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is clinare, to bend, with prefixes fixing the direction of the lean.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 clinare「弯」，前缀决定倾斜的方向。

items.example: The board inclines towards the left.
She has an inclination for drawing.
They were disinclined to move house again.

items.meaning: to lean down, to fall off

items.example: Recline the seat for the long flight.
items.exampleCN: 长途飞行时把座位往后放。

items.meaning: the band of earth where the sun slants
items.example: The climate here is dry and warm.

items.meaning: rising sharply, the extreme of an incline
items.meaningCN: 形容词：陡的，是斜坡的极端
items.exampleCN: 那条陡路把大家都累坏了。

definition_zh: 激励；激发；成为……的动机；说明……的理由
definition_en: to give someone a reason to act; to be the reason that drives an action; and to justify a choice with stated grounds
core_image: 一个人被远方一点亮光吸住，原本停住的脚慢慢迈了出去
scene: 球场边的白板上还留着上一场比赛的圆圈和箭头，教练让队员围拢过来，指着墙上的旧照片讲起从前那场翻盘。 The coach used an old photograph to motivate the players before the final.
sceneCN: 这里是「激励、激发干劲」（第 1 个义项：给人行动的理由）；句意为教练用一张旧照片在决赛前激励队员。图中可辨识物件：白板、旧照片、围成圈的队员。

pos.zh: 激励；激发；成为……的动机；说明理由

derivatives.zh: 由 motivate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「动机；积极性」
由 motivation 加 -al 构成，义为「激励性的；鼓舞人心的」
由 motivate 加表示「人或物」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「激励者；动力因素」
由否定前缀 de- 加 motivate 构成，义为「使失去动力」

senses.title: To give a person a reason to act
senses.definition: to make someone want to do something, especially by giving them a purpose or an incentive
senses.definitionCN: 使人愿意去做某事，尤指通过给其一个目标或动力
senses.example: Good teachers motivate students by making the subject matter feel useful.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师让学生觉得所学有用，从而激励他们。
senses.why: Latin movere meant to set in motion, and this verb was formed on motive, the inner force that starts an action, so motivate is literally to set a person moving from inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 movere 意为「使动起来」，这个动词由 motive（启动行动的内心力量）构成，所以 motivate 字面就是把人从内部推动起来。

senses.title: To be the reason behind an action
senses.definition: to be the reason or cause that makes an action, choice or change happen
senses.definitionCN: 成为使某个行动、选择或变化发生的理由或原因
senses.example: A wish to protect his family motivated the long move to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 想保护家人的愿望促成了他搬去另一座城市，成了这次远迁的动机。
senses.why: Once a motive is understood as an inner force, the verb can also point the other way: the force itself motivates the deed, so the wish, not the person, becomes the subject of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把 motive 理解为一股内在力量，这个动词也能反过来指：那股力量本身促成了行动，于是句子的主语变成愿望本身，而不是人。

senses.title: To set out reasons for a decision
senses.definition: to give reasons for a decision, proposal or statement, especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 为某个决定、提议或说法给出理由，尤用于正式写作
senses.example: The paper motivates its choice of method in a short opening section.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文在开头一小节里为它的方法选择提供了理由。
senses.why: A motive explains why something was done, so the derived verb took on the academic task of setting those reasons out, and motivate acquired the sense of justify.
senses.whyCN: motive 解释一件事为什么被做，于是由它派生的动词接过了学术写作里「把理由摆出来」的任务，motivate 就多了一层「论证、说明理由」的意思。

intro.en: Motivate is a nineteenth-century English coinage built on motive, which came through French from Latin movere, to move.
intro.cn: motivate 是十九世纪英语用 motive 造出来的词，而 motive 经法语来自拉丁语 movere（移动）。

items.en: Movere meant to move or to set in motion, and it supplied the verb behind motion, motive, motor and promote.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来，是 motion、motive、motor、promote 这些词背后的动词。

items.en: Its participle motus, a movement, also worked as a noun, and English later used the same stem for both physical motion and a stated reason.
items.cn: 它的分词 motus 意为「运动」，也可作名词；英语后来用同一个词干兼指身体的运动与陈述出来的理由。

items.en: Motivus meant serving to move, and medieval writers applied it to ideas and arguments that move the will rather than the body.
items.cn: motivus 意为「起推动作用的」，中世纪的作者把它用在能打动意志而非移动身体的念头与论据上。

items.en: Old French motif named a motive or a reason, and English borrowed motive in the fifteenth century as a word for what prompts action.
items.cn: 古法语 motif 指动机或理由，英语在十五世纪借入 motive，用来指促使人行动的东西。

items.en: The verb motivate is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when writers on psychology and education added -ate to motive and used it for the act of supplying a reason.
items.cn: 动词 motivate 一般认为形成于十九世纪，研究心理与教育的作者在 motive 后加 -ate，用它表示「提供理由」这件事。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of moving and its English family; the near-meaning group collects verbs for pushing a person toward action or for supplying grounds.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」动词及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示推动人行动或提供理由的动词。

entries.definition: A reason that makes someone act in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 使人以某种方式行动的理由。

entries.definition: The act or process of moving.
To raise someone to a higher position, or to help something advance.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人提到更高职位，或推动某事进展。

entries.definition: A strong feeling that moves a person.
To give someone confidence or support to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人信心或支持去做某事。

entries.definition: To fill someone with the desire to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人产生做某事的愿望。

entries.definition: To force or push someone into a state or action.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使或推动某人进入某种状态或行动。

entries.definition: To cause someone to do something, often quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 促使某人（往往马上）做某事。

normalIntro.en: The word stands on a Latin verb of moving, and its family keeps returning to the force that starts an action and to the reason given for it afterwards.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语「移动」动词上，同族词反复回到启动行动的那股力，以及事后为行动给出的理由。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and motive names the force that starts the moving, so motivate is to set a person in motion.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，motive 指启动移动的那股力，所以 motivate 就是把人推动起来。

normal.en: The ending -ate turns a noun or adjective into a verb of action, which is how motive became motivate in the nineteenth century.
normal.cn: -ate 这个结尾把名词或形容词变成表示动作的动词，motive 就是这样在十九世纪变成了 motivate。

normal.en: Motivation adds -ion and names the force itself, while motivator adds -or and names the person or thing that supplies it.
normal.cn: motivation 加 -ion，指那股力本身；motivator 加 -or，指提供那股力的人或物。

normal.en: De- reverses the verb, so demotivate is to take the drive away, a word that works because motivate is about a force.
normal.cn: de- 把动词反转，所以 demotivate 就是把动力拿走；这个词讲得通，正因为 motivate 说的是一股力。

normal.en: A coach, a teacher and a bonus can all be subjects of motivate, because the word cares about the reason supplied, not about who supplies it.
normal.cn: 教练、老师和奖金都可以做 motivate 的主语，因为这个词在意的是提供了什么理由，而不是谁来提供。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still until a small light far ahead catches the eye, and the first step follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人原本站着不动，直到远处一点亮光吸住目光，第一步就跟着迈了出去。

abstract.en: A motive is invisible, yet it is the hinge on which a whole day of effort turns, so one small reason can move a large body.
abstract.cn: 动机看不见，却是一整天努力转动的那个铰链，所以一个小理由就能挪动一整个人。

abstract.en: To motivate is to hand someone a reason; to be motivated is to take that reason and make it your own.
abstract.cn: 激励是把一个理由交到别人手上；受到激励，则是接过这个理由并把它变成自己的。

examples.en: Good teachers motivate students by making the subject matter feel useful.
examples.cn: 好老师让学生觉得所学有用，从而激励他们。

examples.en: A wish to protect his family motivated the long move to another city.
examples.cn: 想保护家人的愿望促成了他搬去另一座城市。

examples.en: The paper motivates its choice of method in a short opening section.
examples.cn: 这篇论文在开头一小节里为它的方法选择提供了理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫提为特」——莫提一个理由，就为特地去行动；记住 motivate 是激励、成为动机、说明理由。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）的过去分词 motus 派生出 motivus（推动的），经法语 motif 与英语 motive 后，十九世纪加 -ate 构成 motivate；同族词有 motive、motion、motor、promote、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reason that sets a person moving; the senses divide into supplying that reason, being that reason, and stating reasons in formal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是让人动起来的理由；义项分出提供这股理由、本身成为理由，以及在正式文字里陈述理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing still until a distant light pulls the first step out of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人原本停住，远处一点光把他的第一步拉了出来。

branches.en: a coach turning an old story into a reason to run harder
branches.cn: 教练把一段旧事变成一个更拼命跑的理由

branches.en: a bonus that makes a team arrive early
branches.cn: 一笔让团队提前到岗的奖金

definition_en: to work together with others for a shared aim, or to do what is asked of you
core_image: 两双手同时抬起同一只箱子，脚步踩在一个节拍上
scene: 谁也不肯先动，老师只好请两个小组一起想办法。 The two teams agreed to cooperate on the project.

senses.title: To work together
senses.definition: to join with others in doing something for a shared aim

senses.whyCN: 一双手能抬起的有限，另外两双手抬起剩下的。

intro.en: Cooperate comes from Late Latin cooperari, built from co-, together, and operari, to work, from opus, work.
intro.cn: cooperate 来自晚期拉丁语 cooperari，由 co-（一起）与 operari（工作）构成，词根 opus 意为工作。

items.en: Opus meant work, a task or a piece of labour.
items.cn: opus 意为工作、任务或一份劳动。

items.en: Operari meant to work or to be busy with a task.
items.cn: operari 意为工作或忙于某项任务。

items.en: Cooperari meant to work along with another person.
items.cn: cooperari 意为与另一个人一起工作。

items.en: English cooperate first described working jointly on a task.
items.cn: 英语 cooperate 最初指共同做一项工作。

items.en: The word gained the milder sense of agreeing to help.
items.cn: 这个词又获得了同意协助这一较温和的含义。

items.en: Today it covers teams, machines and even countries.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖团队、机器，甚至国家。
