branches.cn: 活的翅膀与静止的石头都向高处伸展。

intro.en: Soar builds words for flight, height, and rising values.
intro.cn: soar 构成表示飞行、高度和上涨的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source aura meant a breeze.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 aura 意为微风。

items.meaning: to rise high into the air
items.example: The bird soared over the lake.
The kite soars in the wind.
The plane soared above the clouds.

items.exampleCN: 飙升的成本改变了计划。

items.meaning: a person or thing that soars
items.example: The glider is a quiet soarer.
items.exampleCN: 滑翔机是一种安静的翱翔者。

items.meaning: to rise high into the air
items.example: The rocket soared into the sky.
Soaring prices hit small shops first.
items.exampleCN: 飞涨的价格先冲击小商店。

latinEntries.example: Aura is Latin for a breeze.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aura 是拉丁语中的微风。

definition_en: belonging separately to each person or thing mentioned
core_image: 几个人走回各自的门口，每扇门只属于一个人
scene: 会议结束后，两位经理回到了各自的办公室。 After the meeting, the two managers returned to their respective offices.
sceneCN: 这里 respective 是「各自的」（第 1 个义项：分别属于先前提到的人或物）；句意：会议结束后，两位经理各自回到自己的办公室。

senses.title: Belonging to each separately
senses.definition: relating to each of the people or things already mentioned, one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐一与已经提到的每个人或每件事相关的
senses.example: The students returned to their respective classrooms.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们回到了各自的教室。
senses.why: The word began as a relative term meaning looking back to each item, so it pairs things with their own owners.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是关系词，意为逐一回看每一项，因此把事物与各自的所有者配对。

senses.title: Separate rather than shared
senses.definition: used to stress that each item has its own separate one
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调每一项都有自己单独的一份
senses.example: Each team presented its respective plan.
senses.exampleCN: 每支队伍都展示了自己那份方案。
senses.why: If every item looks back to its own partner, the result is a set of separate belongings.
senses.whyCN: 如果每一项都对应自己的伙伴，结果就是一整套各自归属之物。

intro.en: Respective comes from Latin respectivus, looking back, from respicere, to look back at, built on re-, back, and specere, to look.
intro.cn: respective 来自拉丁语 respectivus（回看的），源于 respicere（回看），由 re-（向后）与 specere（看）构成。

items.en: Specere means to look.
items.cn: specere 意为看。

items.en: Respicere means to look back at.
items.cn: respicere 意为回看。

items.en: Respectivus means relating or looking back.
items.cn: respectivus 意为有关联的、回看的。

items.en: Respectif carries the relative sense.
items.cn: respectif 保留「各自相关」的含义。

items.en: Modern English uses respective to pair items with their own owners.
items.cn: 现代英语用 respective 把各项与各自的所有者配对。

note.en: Respective is a pairing adjective, close to respectively and to words for separate ownership.
note.cn: respective 是表示配对的形容词，与 respectively 以及表示各自所有的词相邻。

entries.definition: in the order already mentioned
admiration or a particular point
showing respect
belonging to one person or thing
not shared
belonging to a particular person

normalIntro.en: Respective points back to each item: this one to its owner, that one to its owner.
normalIntro.cn: respective 逐一回指每一项：这个对应它的主人，那个对应它的主人。

normal.en: Their respective rooms means each person's own room.
normal.cn: their respective rooms 指每个人的房间。

normal.en: Respective roles are the roles each person has.
normal.cn: respective roles 是每个人各自承担的角色。

normal.en: The adverb respectively keeps the same order.
normal.cn: 副词 respectively 保持同样的顺序。

normal.en: Respective never means respectful.
normal.cn: respective 绝不表示「恭敬的」。

normal.en: Compare separate: separate stresses division, respective stresses matching each item.
normal.cn: 对比 separate：separate 强调分开，respective 强调逐项对应。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking to two different doors.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人走向两扇不同的门。

abstract.en: Imagine two name tags placed on two different chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个名牌分别放在两把不同的椅子上。

abstract.en: Think of two arrows pointing to two separate boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象两个箭头分别指向两个不同的盒子。

examples.en: The two sides set out their respective views.
examples.cn: 双方各自陈述了自己的观点。

examples.en: Each member returned to their respective seat.
examples.cn: 每位成员都回到了各自的座位。

examples.en: The report compares the respective costs of the two plans.
examples.cn: 报告比较了两个方案各自的成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respect + ive」——每个人都被「单独看一眼」，就是各自的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）＋ specere（看）→ respicere（回看）→ respectivus（有关的）→ 英语 respective，核心义「逐一对应、各自归属」。

sensesIntro.en: Respective first pairs each mentioned item with its own owner, and then stresses that these owners are separate.
sensesIntro.cn: respective 先把提到的每一项与自己的所有者配对，再强调这些所有者彼此分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arrows from each item to its own owner.
core.cn: 核心意象：从每一项指向其各自所有者的箭头。

branches.en: Pairing each item with its owner is the core sense.
branches.cn: 把每一项与所有者配对是核心义项。

branches.en: Separateness is the emphasis the adjective often carries.
branches.cn: 分开是这个词常带的强调。

branches.en: Each has a separate item, and each item belongs to its own person.
branches.cn: 每人有单独的一份，每份又属于各自的人。

branches.en: The pair may be two people, two plans, or two rooms.
branches.cn: 配对对象可以是两个人、两个方案或两个房间。

branches.en: Even when the items look alike, they remain respective ones.
branches.cn: 即使物品看起来相似，它们仍是各自的东西。

intro.en: Respective belongs to the specere family of looking words, with English respect, respectful, and respectively.
intro.cn: respective 属于 specere（看）词族，英语亲属有 respect、respectful 与 respectively。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere means to look, and respicere means to look back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 意为看，respicere 意为回看。

definition_zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服
definition_en: to be widespread or dominant, to win out over opposition, or to persuade someone to act
core_image: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下
scene: 山口的风整日不停，一面旧旗被吹得贴住旗杆，却始终没有倒下。 Westerly winds prevail over the pass for most of the year.
sceneCN: 这里指风与天气长期占主导（第 1 个义项：风与天气盛行）；句意为西风一年中大部分时间控制着这个山口。图中可辨识物件：山口、旧旗、旗杆、被风压弯的草；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 盛行；普遍存在；占上风；获胜；说服

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「盛行的；普遍的」
由「盛行」的形容词加名词尾构成，义为「盛行；普遍程度」
由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「占优势的；盛行的」
由「占优势的」形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「占优势地」
与拉丁语「valere」同族，经法语进入英语，义为「有用；有帮助」

senses.title: Of wind and weather
senses.definition: to blow steadily or to be the usual weather of a place and season
senses.definitionCN: 指风持续地吹，或成为某地某季的常况
senses.example: Dry winds prevail across the plateau in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季高原上盛行干燥的风。
senses.why: The earliest English uses describe forces that hold the air, because prevailing is first about what dominates a place.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的用法描述控制空气的力量，因为「盛行」首先指在某地占主导。

senses.title: Of customs and ideas
senses.definition: to be widely found or generally accepted among a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 在一群人中广泛存在或被普遍接受
senses.example: The custom still prevails in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然盛行。
senses.why: Once a usage holds a region the way weather does, the verb extends from air to habit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一种做法像天气那样占住一个地区，这个动词就从空气扩展到习惯。

senses.title: To win an argument
senses.definition: to prove stronger than the opposing case in a debate or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论或争执中证明比对方的主张更强
senses.example: Common sense prevailed after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，常理占了上风。
senses.why: Being stronger is the core of the Latin verb, and an argument is a contest of strength between claims.
senses.whyCN: 「更强」是拉丁动词的核心，而争论正是各种主张之间的力量较量。

senses.title: To win a contest
senses.definition: to defeat opponents in a match, a race or a struggle
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞速或斗争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side prevailed in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在最后几分钟取胜。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal and military verb for the side that turns out stronger.
senses.whyCN: 体育界借用了这个法律与军事动词，指最终更强的一方。

senses.title: To persuade someone
senses.definition: to bring someone round to a course of action by argument or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 通过论证或请求使某人接受某种做法
senses.example: She prevailed on the committee to reopen the case.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服委员会重新审理此案。
senses.why: Persuasion is winning a person over, so the preposition on marks the one who is overcome.
senses.whyCN: 说服就是把一个人争取过来，因此搭配的介词标出被说服的那一方。

senses.title: Of effort that succeeds at last
senses.definition: to succeed after sustained pressure, patience or repeated attempts
senses.definitionCN: 在持续施压、耐心等待或反复尝试之后取得成功
senses.example: Patience and evidence finally prevailed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心与证据最终奏效。
senses.why: The verb can name an impersonal force that wins, even when no person is doing the winning.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以指一种非人的力量取胜，即使并没有人在取胜。

senses.title: Of an old rule that outlives its reason
senses.titleCN: 旧制度延续而缘由已失
senses.definition: to remain in force long after the purpose it once served has disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 在当初的用途消失很久之后仍然有效
senses.example: The old rule still prevails long after its purpose vanished.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧规定在用途消失很久后仍然有效。
senses.why: What prevails simply holds its ground, whether or not anyone can still explain why.
senses.whyCN: 「盛行」的东西只是守住自己的位置，不管还有没有人能解释缘由。

senses.title: To win in a court of law
senses.definition: to succeed in a legal action or to establish a right against the other party
senses.definitionCN: 在法律诉讼中成功，或对另一方确立一项权利
senses.example: The tenant prevailed in the housing dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 租户在住房纠纷中胜诉。
senses.why: Legal language keeps the old sense of a stronger claim carrying the day.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言保留了旧义，即更强的主张最终获胜。

intro.en: Prevail comes from Latin prae-, before or beyond, and valere, to be strong or to be worth, forming praevalere, to be stronger. English took it through French in the fourteenth century; the family of valere also includes valid, value and avail.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语前缀「prae-」「在前、超出」与「valere」「强、有价值」，合成「praevalere」「更强」。英语于十四世纪经法语引入；「valere」的同族词还包括「valid」「value」「avail」。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or to be worth, and it described health, power and value alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为强壮或有价值，同时描述健康、力量与价值。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or beyond, marking a position ahead of others.
items.cn: 前缀意为「在前」或「超出」，标出比别人更靠前的位置。

items.en: Prae plus valere gave praevalere, to be stronger, whose past stem is praevaluī.
items.cn: 前缀加动词得到「praevalere」「更强」，其过去词干为「praevaluī」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English, where it was spelled and pronounced in several ways before settling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带到英语，其拼写与读音经过几种形式才固定下来。

items.en: English used prevail first for holding power or influence, and soon for winning a contest.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词表示掌握权力或影响力，很快也用于表示在较量中获胜。

items.en: Courts fixed the sense of winning a case, while ordinary speech kept the weather, custom and persuasion senses.
items.cn: 法庭固定了「胜诉」义，而日常口语保留了天气、习俗与说服诸义。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like prevail; the second group names neighbouring ideas of dominance, victory and persuasion.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「prevail」相近；第二组是与「支配、取胜、说服」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is dominant or most common, as in the prevailing wind.
entries.definitionCN: 指占主导或最常见的形容词，如盛行风。

entries.definition: Widespread in a place or at a time, often used of diseases or beliefs.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地某时广泛存在的，常用于疾病或观念。

entries.definition: The fact or degree of being widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在的事实或程度。

entries.definition: To be useful or helpful; it shares the Latin strength word.
entries.definitionCN: 指有用、有帮助；共用同一个拉丁「强」词。

entries.definition: Bravery in battle, from the same Latin word for strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指战斗中的勇猛，出自同一个表示力量的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To hold the most power or influence in a place or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地或某种情境中掌握最大的权力或影响。

entries.definition: To be the largest or most noticeable element among others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在其他要素中数量最多或最显著。

entries.definition: To win a decisive victory, often with a sense of celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 指取得决定性胜利，常带庆祝意味。

entries.definition: To convince someone to believe or do something.
entries.definitionCN: 指说服某人相信或去做某事。

entries.definition: To continue in existence or action, close to the sense of an old rule still holding.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续存在或继续行动，接近旧规定仍然有效那一义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin strength word behind prevail, its real family and its fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后表示「强」的拉丁词、真实同族词与固定搭配。

normal.en: Praemia and prevail share a Latin idea: the stronger thing stands, and the stronger claim wins.
normal.cn: 奖品与盛行共享一个拉丁观念：更强的东西站住，更强的主张获胜。

normal.en: The prefix means before or beyond, and the stem means strong, so prevail is to be stronger than what stands in front.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在前、超出」，词干意为「强」，所以这个词指比挡在前面的东西更强。

normal.en: Prevail on someone is the fixed pattern for persuasion, with the preposition on before the person.
normal.cn: 劝说某人用的是固定模式，介词放在人前面。

normal.en: The prevailing wind is the weather phrase, and it is the oldest kind of use.
normal.cn: 盛行风是天气方面的说法，也是最古老的一类用法。

normal.en: Valid, value and avail all descend from the same Latin word for being strong or worth something.
normal.cn: 有效的、价值与有用都出自同一个表示「强或有价值」的拉丁词。

abstract.en: Prevailing is not shouting loudest; it is being the thing that is still standing when the wind drops.
abstract.cn: 盛行不是喊得最响，而是风停之后仍然立着的那一个。

abstract.en: An old rule prevails because nobody remembers how to remove it, not because it is right.
abstract.cn: 旧规定之所以延续，是因为没人记得怎样废除它，而不是因为它正确。

abstract.en: To prevail is to make the world agree with you without having to raise your voice.
abstract.cn: 占上风是让世界同意你，而不必提高嗓门。

examples.en: Cooler air will prevail over the region by the weekend.
examples.cn: 到周末，较凉的空气将控制这一地区。

examples.en: The older interpretation prevailed among historians for a century.
examples.cn: 较旧的解释在历史学家中盛行了整整一个世纪。

examples.en: They tried to prevail on the minister to change the policy.
examples.cn: 他们试图说服部长改变这项政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞威尔」——「普」遍都「瑞」气「威」风，处处占上风：盛行、取胜、说服。

root: 拉丁语「prae-」「在前、超出」加「valere」「强、有价值」构成「praevalere」「更强」，其过去词干为「praevaluī」；英语十四世纪经法语引入；「valere」同族有「valid」「value」「avail」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from wind holding a place, to a custom being widespread, an argument or contest won, a person persuaded, effort succeeding, an old rule surviving, and a case won in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从风占住一地，走向习俗广布、争论或较量取胜、说服某人、努力奏效、旧制度延续，以及法律上胜诉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag that bends in a steady gale but never falls, because the stronger force holds its ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面旗在稳定的大风里被压弯却从不倒下，因为更强的力量守住了位置。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: one wind or one kind of weather holds a place for most of the year.
branches.cn: 天气：一种风或一类天气在一年的大部分时间里占住一个地方。

branches.en: THE LONG HABIT: a custom spreads widely, and an old rule stays after its reason is gone.
branches.cn: 长久的习惯：习俗广泛流传，旧规定在缘由消失后仍留下。

branches.en: THE STRONGER CLAIM: an argument wins out, and a side wins the match.
branches.cn: 更强的主张：一种论点占上风，一方赢下比赛。

branches.en: THE OVERCOMING: a person is persuaded, and patient effort succeeds at last.
branches.cn: 争取与奏效：一个人被说服，耐心的努力最终成功。

branches.en: THE COURT: the stronger legal right carries the case.
branches.cn: 法庭：更强的法律权利赢得案件。

intro.en: Prevail is a Latin verb built from a prefix of position and a stem of strength, and English keeps both pieces in a whole family.
intro.cn: 这是一个由位置前缀与力量词干构成的拉丁动词，英语在两个成分上都保留了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere supplies the strength, prae- supplies the advantage, and praevalere joins them into one verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「valere」提供力量，「prae-」提供优势，「praevalere」把两者合成一个动词。

items.example: It marks the position of being ahead of others.
items.exampleCN: 它标出比别人更靠前的位置。

items.meaning: to be strong, to be worth
items.example: The stem carries health, power and worth together.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干同时带着健康、力量与价值。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English shortened the Latin verb into its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个拉丁动词缩短成现代形态。

items.example: It describes the wind or the mood of a time.
items.exampleCN: 它描述风或一个时期的风气。

items.example: It applies to diseases, beliefs and customs.
items.exampleCN: 它适用于疾病、观念与习俗。

items.example: Epidemiologists measure it as a rate.
items.exampleCN: 流行病学家把它当作一个比率来测量。

items.example: It forms the adjective from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它从动词词干构成形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a noun.

由「盛行」的形容词加名词尾构成，义为「盛行；普遍程度」
由该动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「占优势的；盛行的」

与拉丁语「valere」同族，义为「有效的；正当的」

definition_en: to pass a device over something, to look through quickly, or to examine closely
core_image: 一束光在纸面上来回移动，把文字变成电脑里的图像
scene: 医生把片子放进机器里扫描。 The doctor scanned the image for problems.
sceneCN: 这里 scan 是「扫描」（第 1 个义项）；句意：医生扫描图像查找问题。

senses.title: Use a scanning device
senses.definition: to pass a machine or beam over something to read or record it
senses.definitionCN: 让机器或光束掠过某物以读取或记录
senses.example: Please scan the barcode at the till.
senses.exampleCN: 请在收银台扫描条形码。
senses.why: The core sense is a moving beam that captures a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是移动的光束捕捉一个表面。

senses.title: Look through quickly
senses.definition: to read or look through something quickly
senses.definitionCN: 快速阅读或查看某物
senses.example: I scanned the menu and chose soup.
senses.exampleCN: 我浏览菜单，选了汤。
senses.why: The eye sweeps the page like a scanning beam.
senses.whyCN: 目光像扫描光束一样掠过页面。

senses.title: Examine closely
senses.definition: to examine something carefully in search of details
senses.definitionCN: 仔细检查某物以寻找细节
senses.example: He scanned her face for a sign.
senses.exampleCN: 他审视她的脸寻找迹象。
senses.why: A slow scan searches every part of the surface.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢扫描会探查表面的每个部分。

senses.title: Mark verse metre
senses.definition: to mark the stressed and unstressed beats of a poem
senses.definitionCN: 标出诗句中的重读与非重读音步
senses.example: Students scanned the lines of Latin verse.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们标出拉丁诗句的格律。
senses.why: The old sense is climbing through a line beat by beat.
senses.whyCN: 古老义项是逐拍走过一行诗。

senses.title: Medical image
senses.definition: a medical test that produces an image of the inside of the body
senses.definitionCN: 生成身体内部图像的医学检查
senses.example: The scan showed a small fracture.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处小骨折。
senses.why: The device action becomes the name of the test.
senses.whyCN: 设备动作转化为检查的名称。

intro.en: Scan comes from Latin scandere, to climb, which also meant to scan verse.
intro.cn: scan 源自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），也指逐拍分析诗句。

items.en: Scandere means to climb or mount.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀登、上升。

items.en: Scansion named the marking of verse rhythm.
items.cn: scansion 指标记诗句节奏。

items.en: Scanning verse meant moving through each foot.
items.cn: 分析诗句意味着逐个音步走过。

items.en: Scanen meant to examine verse closely.
items.cn: scanen 意为仔细分析诗句。

items.en: The word extended to beams and medical imaging.
items.cn: 该词扩展到光束与医学成像。

note.en: Scan is compared with similar spellings and with other ways of looking.
note.cn: 把 scan 与形近词以及其它观看方式作比较。

a dishonest plan for money
a mark left by a wound
to read quickly for the main idea
to look at something closely
to move quickly over an area

normalIntro.en: Scan joins the idea of climbing through verse with sweeping a beam over a surface.
normalIntro.cn: scan 把逐拍走过诗句与光束扫过表面联系起来。

normal.en: A scanner sweeps a line of light across the page.
normal.cn: 扫描仪让一条光扫过页面。

normal.en: To scan a menu is to sweep your eyes down it fast.
normal.cn: scan 菜单就是目光快速向下扫过。

normal.en: The double n appears in scanned and scanning.
normal.cn: scanned 和 scanning 中都有双写 n。

normal.en: A brain scan is a picture made by scanning.
normal.cn: 脑部扫描是由扫描生成的图像。

normal.en: Scan the crowd means searching faces quickly.
normal.cn: scan the crowd 意为快速搜寻人脸。

abstract.en: Scanning turns a surface into information.
abstract.cn: 扫描把一个表面转化为信息。

abstract.en: Fast looking finds the shape; slow scanning finds the detail.
abstract.cn: 快速浏览找到轮廓，缓慢扫描找到细节。

abstract.en: The beam and the eye both move in lines.
abstract.cn: 光束和目光都以线条移动。

examples.en: She scanned the receipt into the computer.
examples.cn: 她把收据扫描进电脑。

examples.en: He scanned the report for any mention of cost.
examples.cn: 他快速浏览报告寻找有关成本的提及。

examples.en: The guard scanned the crowd at the gate.
examples.cn: 警卫在门口扫视人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: scan 原指「一步步攀登」诗句的格律，后来引申为光束一行行扫过，即扫描；再引申为目光快速浏览。

root: 源自拉丁语 scandere（攀登），经「逐拍分析诗行」引申为扫视、扫描，核心义「一行行地掠过」。

sensesIntro.en: Scan means to use a beam or machine, to look through quickly, to examine closely, or a medical image.
sensesIntro.cn: scan 意为用光束或机器扫描、快速浏览、仔细审视，或医学扫描检查。

core.en: To move steadily across a surface, as a beam or an eye.
core.cn: 像光束或目光一样稳定地掠过表面。

branches.en: A device sweeps and records a surface.
branches.cn: 设备掠过并记录表面。

branches.en: The eye sweeps text for key points.
branches.cn: 目光掠过文字抓取要点。

branches.en: The eye moves slowly to catch details.
branches.cn: 目光缓慢移动以捕捉细节。

branches.en: The old sense of walking through verse beats.
branches.cn: 逐拍走过诗句的古老义项。

branches.en: The action of scanning produces a medical scan.
branches.cn: 扫描动作产生了医学扫描检查。

intro.en: Scan has a small but active family in technology and poetry.
intro.cn: scan 在技术与诗歌领域有一个小而活跃的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb scandere, to climb, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 scandere（攀登）是远源。

items.meaning: to sweep over or a medical test

latinEntries.meaning: a climbing or scanning of verse

definition_en: to rise up against a ruler or refuse to accept something
core_image: 广场上的人群举起手，旗帜在风里翻卷
scene: 粮价上涨后，城里的居民起来反抗，要求罢免官员。 After the price of grain rose, the townspeople revolted and demanded the removal of the officials.
sceneCN: 这里 revolt 是「起义、反抗」（第 1 个义项：起来反对统治者）；句意：粮价上涨后，城里的居民起来反抗，要求罢免官员。

senses.title: Rising against a ruler
senses.definition: to take violent action against a government
senses.definitionCN: 对政府采取暴力行动
senses.example: The peasants revolted against the heavy taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 农民反抗沉重的赋税。
senses.why: The Latin root volv means to roll, as a crowd rolls against authority.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 volv 意为滚动，人群如浪潮般涌向权威。

senses.title: Strong disgust
senses.definition: to feel strong disgust at something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事感到强烈厌恶
senses.example: She revolted at the sight of the dirty kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 看到肮脏的厨房，她感到厌恶。
senses.why: The mind can turn away as violently as a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 内心的抗拒可以像人群一样激烈地转向。

senses.title: A rebellion
senses.definition: an act of rising against authority
senses.definitionCN: 反对权威的行动
senses.example: The revolt was crushed within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这场起义一周内就被镇压了。
senses.why: The verb's action becomes a named event.
senses.whyCN: 动词的行为变成了一个有名称的事件。

intro.en: Revolt comes from French revolter, from Italian rivoltare, to turn over.
intro.cn: revolt 源自法语 revolter，再往前是意大利语 rivoltare（翻转）。

items.en: Revolvere joins re-, back, to volvere, to roll.
items.cn: revolvere 由 re-（回）与 volvere（滚）组成。

items.en: Rivoltare means to turn over or throw back.
items.cn: rivoltare 意为翻转或掷回。

items.en: Revolter brings the word into French.
items.cn: revolter 把词带入法语。

items.en: Revolt first means to turn away from a ruler.
items.cn: revolt 最初指背离统治者。

items.en: It also names the uprising itself.
items.cn: 它也指起义事件本身。

note.en: Revolt is a turning away; revolution is a full turning around.
note.cn: revolt 是转开，revolution 是彻底转一圈。

entries.definition: a handgun with a turning cylinder
to turn around a center
a complete change of government
to fight against authority
a rising against rulers
to oppose something

normalIntro.en: Revolt is a crowd rolling back against authority.
normalIntro.cn: revolt 是人群掉头涌向权威。

normal.en: Revolt against a ruler means rise up.
normal.cn: revolt against a ruler 意为起来反抗。

normal.en: An armed revolt uses weapons.
normal.cn: an armed revolt 使用武器。

normal.en: Revolt at something means feel disgust.
normal.cn: revolt at something 意为感到厌恶。

normal.en: Crush a revolt means end it by force.
normal.cn: crush a revolt 意为以武力结束起义。

normal.en: Compare rebel: a rebel acts, a revolt is the rising.
normal.cn: 对比 rebel：rebel 指人行动，revolt 指起义本身。

abstract.en: Picture a flag turning against the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一面逆风翻卷的旗帜。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave rolling back toward the shore it came from.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪朝来时的岸边涌回。

abstract.en: Think of a door pushed shut by many hands at once.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手同时把门推上。

examples.en: The workers revolted against the new rules.
examples.cn: 工人们反抗新规定。

examples.en: The smell made him revolt.
examples.cn: 那气味让他感到厌恶。

examples.en: The revolt spread through the northern towns.
examples.cn: 起义蔓延到北方城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ volt（转）」——掉头转向权威，就是反抗、起义。

root: 拉丁语 revolvere（翻滚回去）＝ re-（回）＋ volvere（滚）→ 意大利语 rivoltare → 法语 revolter → revolt。

sensesIntro.en: Revolt begins as rising against a ruler, then describes inner disgust, and finally names the uprising itself.
sensesIntro.cn: revolt 先指起来反抗统治者，再描述内心的厌恶，最后指起义事件本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with raised hands and a flag in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：举手的人群与风中翻卷的旗帜。

branches.en: Rising against a ruler is the core.
branches.cn: 反抗统治者是核心含义。

branches.en: The mind turns away in disgust.
branches.cn: 内心因厌恶而转开。

branches.en: The rising becomes a named event.
branches.cn: 起义成为有名称的事件。

branches.en: The action and the event share one word.
branches.cn: 行为与事件共用一个词。

branches.en: Disgust and rebellion both mean turning away.
branches.cn: 厌恶与叛乱都意味着转开。

intro.en: Revolt combines re-, back, with the Latin root volv, to roll.
intro.cn: revolt 由 re-（回）与拉丁词根 volv（滚）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere, to roll, explains the rolling movement of a crowd.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere（滚）解释了人群如浪潮般的滚动。

items.example: Rivoltare brings the word toward French.
Revolter is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: revolter 是直接的法语来源。
revolting 描述令人厌恶的事物。

latinEntries.exampleCN: volvere 是 revolve 与 revolt 的基础。
revolvere 发展出意大利语 rivoltare。

definition_en: a narrow band used to fasten or carry something, or to fasten something with such a band
core_image: 一条绕过箱子、被扣紧的宽皮带
scene: 他用一条皮带把箱子绑紧。 He tightened the strap around the box.
sceneCN: 这里 strap 是「带子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用一条皮带把箱子绑紧。

senses.title: A fastening band
senses.definition: a narrow band used to fasten or carry something
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆扎或承提物品的窄带
senses.example: He tightened the strap around the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: A worn band
senses.definition: a band worn over the shoulder or around the wrist
senses.definitionCN: 挂在肩上或绕在腕上的带子
senses.example: Her shoulder strap slipped.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肩带滑了下来。
senses.why: The same band is worn rather than tied.
senses.whyCN: 同一类带子从捆扎变成了穿戴。

senses.title: Fasten with a strap
senses.definition: to fasten something with a strap
senses.definitionCN: 用带子把某物固定住
senses.example: Strap the bag to the bike.
senses.exampleCN: 把包绑在自行车上。
senses.why: The noun turns into the action it allows.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为它所带来的动作。

intro.en: Strap travelled from Greek through Latin and French.
intro.cn: strap 从希腊语经拉丁语与法语传入英语。

items.en: Strophos meant a twisted band.
items.cn: strophos 指扭成的带子。

items.en: Stroppus meant a thong.
items.cn: stroppus 指皮条。

items.en: Estrop meant a loop or band.
items.cn: estrop 指环或带。

items.en: Strap named a narrow band.
items.cn: strap 指窄带。

items.en: Strap became a verb for fastening.
items.cn: strap 成为表示捆扎的动词。

note.en: Strap is compared with look-alike words and with words for bands and belts.
note.cn: 把 strap 与形近词以及表示带子和皮带的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A strap holds things together so they can travel.
normalIntro.cn: strap 把东西绑在一起，好让它们上路。

normal.en: He tightened the strap around the box.
normal.cn: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。

normal.en: Strap the bag to the bike.
normal.cn: 把包绑在自行车上。

normal.en: Her shoulder strap slipped.
normal.cn: 她的肩带滑了下来。

normal.en: The watch strap is worn.
normal.cn: 表带旧了。

normal.en: Strap in before we start.
normal.cn: 出发前系好安全带。

abstract.en: A strap is a promise that nothing will be dropped.
abstract.cn: 带子，是一个不让东西掉下去的承诺。

abstract.en: What is strapped down can still be carried far.
abstract.cn: 绑稳的东西，才能被带到很远。

abstract.en: Some burdens are lightened by a good strap.
abstract.cn: 有些重担，会被一条好带子分担。

examples.en: He tightened the strap around the box.
examples.cn: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。

examples.en: Strap the bag to the bike.
examples.cn: 把包绑在自行车上。

examples.en: Her shoulder strap slipped.

dict_mnemonic.text: strap 是「带子」，也作动词表示「用带子捆扎」；shoulder strap 是肩带，watch strap 是表带，strap in 是系好安全带。

root: 经古法语 estrop 来自拉丁语 stroppus（皮条），更早可追溯至希腊语 strophos（扭成的带子）；由窄带，引申为用带子捆扎的动作。

sensesIntro.en: Strap is a fastening band, a worn band, or to fasten with a band.
sensesIntro.cn: strap 是捆扎用的带子、穿戴的带子，或用带子捆扎。

core.en: A narrow strip that holds things.
core.cn: 一条把东西拢住的窄带。

branches.en: He tightened the strap around the box.
branches.cn: 他把箱子上的带子勒紧。

branches.en: Her shoulder strap slipped.
branches.cn: 她的肩带滑了下来。

branches.en: Strap the bag to the bike.
branches.cn: 把包绑在自行车上。

branches.en: The band and the binding are one action.
branches.cn: 带子与捆扎，本就是一件事。

branches.en: What you wear and what you tie share a word.
branches.cn: 你穿戴的和你绑上的，共用同一个词。

intro.en: Strap doubles its final letter and builds words for bands.
intro.cn: strap 变化时双写词尾，并构成与带子相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source stroppus meant a thong.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 stroppus 指皮条。
